This is the step the manuscript writes as "group `F = [...] + [...]`", and it is an identity for any `f` whatever — no property of `x^(3/2)` is used.
declarations.name: lemma51iii_regroup

declarations.doc: The corner floors satisfy `⌊A + B + ε⌋ - ⌊A⌋ - ⌊B⌋ ∈ {-1, 0, 1, 2}` whenever `|ε| < 1`. Here `A = Δ₁X`, `B = Δ₂X` and `ε = ΔΔX`, so this is the step that needs `|ΔΔX| < 1`.
declarations.name: corner_floor_range

declarations.doc: **`|j| ≤ 3`.** The net offset `j = β₁₂ - β₁ - β₂` combines the corner floor range with the three level-1 carries `κ ∈ {0,1}³`.
declarations.name: offset_abs_le_three

declarations.doc: `β = ⌊ΔX⌋ + κ = ⌊ΔX + θ⌋`: the level-1 carry is `⌊{ΔX} + θ⌋`.
declarations.name: carry_eq_floor_shifted

declarations.doc: **`-1 ≤ j ≤ 2`.** `j = ⌊A+B+ε+θ⌋ - ⌊A+θ⌋ - ⌊B+θ⌋` is `corner_floor_range` at `(A+θ, B+θ, ε-θ)`, and `|ε - θ| < 1` whenever `0 < ε < 1` and `0 ≤ θ < 1`.
declarations.name: offset_range_with_carries

declarations.doc: **`|j| ≤ 2`**, replacing the printed `|j| ≤ 3`.
declarations.name: offset_abs_le_two

declarations.doc: **`|ΔΔX| < 1`**, the hypothesis the offset bound needs. With shifts `d₁ = 2h₁`, `d₂ = 2h₂`, `|ΔΔX| ≤ d₁d₂ sup|X''| = 4h₁h₂·(3/4)P^(-1/2)`, so the condition is exactly the manuscript's `h₁h₂ ≤ P^(1/2)/3` — stated here with `q = P^(1/2)` and strict inequality.
declarations.name: double_difference_lt_one

declarations.doc: **The `β`-product bound.** From `β_i ≤ 3√2 h_i q + 1` with `q = P^(1/2)`, `h_i ≥ 1` and `q ≥ 10`, the product satisfies `β₁β₂ ≤ 19 h₁h₂ q²`, which is what the manuscript carries: `(3√2)² = 18` is the product of the leading terms, and the `+1`s take it to `19`. `4.25 ≥ 3√2` is the rational substitute. Not an over-quantification, though it separates two variables one `n` determines: both factors are extremal at the same `n = 2P`, `β₁β₂/(h₁h₂P)` attains `18` exactly, and `4.25² = 18.0625` is the whole of the loss. See the note at Lemma 5.1(iii) and `decoration_budget.beta_inventory_attained`.
declarations.name: beta_product_bound

declarations.doc: `3√2 ≤ 4.25`, the rational substitute used above.
declarations.name: three_sqrt_two_le

declarations.doc: **The `β`-part of `G'`.** `(9/16)β₁β₂ s^(-7) ≤ 20 h₁h₂ p^(-3)`, the printed `20 h₁h₂P^(-3/4)`; the constant used is `(9/16)·19 = 10.6875 ≤ 20`.
declarations.name: Gprime_beta_bound

declarations.doc: **The cancellation in `G''`.** `G'' = F''(X)(X')² + F'(X)X''`, and the two `β`-contributions have opposite signs: `81/64` from the first and `-9/32` from the second, leaving `63/64`.
declarations.name: Gsecond_beta_cancellation

declarations.doc: **The printed `25` needs that cancellation.** With `β₁β₂ ≤ 19 h₁h₂P`, the combined coefficient `63/64` gives `18.7 ≤ 25`; bounding the two `β`-terms separately gives `99/64`, i.e. `29.4`, which exceeds `25`. The manuscript's bound is correct, but its naive derivation is not.
declarations.name: Gsecond_naive_bound_fails

declarations.doc: **The `β`-part of `G''`.** `(63/64)β₁β₂ s^(-11) ≤ 25 h₁h₂ p^(-7)`, the printed `25 h₁h₂P^(-7/4)`.
declarations.name: Gsecond_beta_bound

declarations.doc: **The `j`-part of `G''`.** `(9/32)|j| s^(-5) ≤ 2|j| p^(-5)`, the printed `2|j|P^(-5/4)`; here too the two contributions cancel, `-27/32 + 9/16 = -9/32`.
declarations.name: Gsecond_j_bound

declarations.doc: **The offset term.** `(3/2)|j|A^(1/2)` with `P^(3/2) ≤ A ≤ 3.004 P^(3/2)` lies in `[1.5|j|P^(3/4), 2.6|j|P^(3/4)]`. Written with `w = A^(1/2)` and `p = P^(1/4)`, the hypothesis is `p³ ≤ w ≤ 1.7333 p³`; the manuscript's `2^(3/2)` gives `w ≤ 1.6818 p³`, so `2.6` has room.
declarations.name: offset_term_bounds

declarations.doc: **The second-difference term.** `(3/4)β₁β₂B^(-1/2)` with `9 h₁h₂P ≤ β₁β₂ ≤ 19 h₁h₂P` and `p³ ≤ u ≤ 1.7333 p³` (where `u = B^(1/2)`) lies in `[1.4 h₁h₂P^(1/4), 15 h₁h₂P^(1/4)]`: the lower end is `(3/4)·9/1.7333 = 3.89 ≥ 1.4`, the upper `(3/4)·19 = 14.25 ≤ 15`.
declarations.name: second_difference_term_bounds

declarations.doc: **The run-length arithmetic.** With `A = 2|j|p^(-1)` and `B = 20 h₁h₂ p^(-3)`, and `M = max((|j|+1)p^(-1), h₁h₂p^(-3))`, one has `A ≤ 2M` and `B ≤ 20M`, so `A + B ≤ 22M`. The `22` of the manuscript is exactly `2 + 20`.
declarations.name: run_length_arithmetic

declarations.doc: **The run-length conclusion.** If `G` moves at rate at most `22M`, then over an interval of length `1/(22M)` it moves by at most `1`, so `⌊G⌋` takes at most two values there: runs of `⌊G(n)⌋` have length at least `(1/22)min(P^(1/4)/(|j|+1), P^(3/4)/(h₁h₂))`.
declarations.name: run_length_conclusion

The kill tables verify the numeric failure of this inequality per surviving length; that evaluation stays verified computation, the implication is Lean.

declarations.doc: At the base point `m = n^(3/2)`, `v = n^(9/4)` every term is a multiple of `n^(27/8)` and the six coefficients sum to `1`: the expansion reproduces `v^(3/2)` exactly there.
declarations.name: stepB_exact_at_base

declarations.doc: The `m`-derivative vanishes at the base point. It must: `v^(3/2)` does not depend on `m`, so the printed expansion would be wrong if it did not.

declarations.doc: The total smooth `v`-coefficient is `(3/2) n^(9/8)`, so the monomial weight of Theorem 5.3 is `c = (3k/4) nu^(9/8)`. This is the identity printed in Step B.
declarations.name: stepB_v_coefficient

declarations.doc: The `m`-block, rewritten in `e`, is `-1/2 - (9/8)e - (45/64)e^2`.
declarations.name: stepB_m_block_in_epsilon

declarations.name: stepB_v_block_in_epsilon

declarations.doc: The `m`-block is the degree-2 Taylor polynomial of `-(1/2)(1+e)^(9/4)`: binomial coefficients `1, 9/4, (9/4)(5/4)/2 = 45/32` scaled by `-1/2`.
declarations.name: stepB_m_block_is_taylor

declarations.doc: The `v`-coefficient block is the degree-2 Taylor polynomial of `(3/2)(1+e)^(3/4)`: binomial coefficients `1, 3/4, (3/4)(-1/4)/2 = -3/32` scaled by `3/2`.
declarations.name: stepB_v_block_is_taylor

declarations.doc: The structural identity behind all of it: with `t2 = m^(3/2) - v`, `v^(3/2) = m^(9/4) - (3/2) m^(3/4) t2 + O(m^(-3/4))`, and eliminating `t2` gives `-(1/2) m^(9/4) + (3/2) m^(3/4) v`. Here as an identity in the two blocks, `M` standing for `m^(3/4)`, so that `m^(3/2) = M^2` and `m^(9/4) = M^3`.
declarations.name: stepB_structure

declarations.doc: Offset branches. The frozen-shape offset monomial `(9/8) k j nu^(15/8)` has curvature `(9/8)(15/8)(7/8) = 945/512`, the frozen kernel anchor is `27/16 = 864/512`, and the surviving offset is the difference `81/512`.
declarations.name: stepE_offset_survivor

declarations.doc: The total `theta`-coefficient `B = (27/32) k j nu^(3/8)` is `3/2` times the bare-kernel value `9/16`, and is not the moving-gap value `45/32`.
declarations.name: stepE_B_ratio

declarations.doc: The window-centre mode carries `B * X'' = (27/32)(3/4) = 81/128 = 324/512`, and the offset composite is single-signed: `81/512 - 324/512 = -243/512 <> 0`.
declarations.name: stepE_offset_composite

declarations.doc: The printed range `lambda_a' in [0.40, 0.52] k|j| P^(-1/8)` holds on a dyadic block: `243/512 = 0.4746` and `nu^(-1/8)` ranges over `[2^(-1/8), 1)`, inside `[0.917, 1]`.
declarations.name: stepE_lambda_a_range

declarations.doc: Zero-offset branches. `lambda_0' = (1095/1024) k h1 h2 nu^(-5/8)` and `nu^(-5/8)` ranges over `[2^(-5/8), 1)`, inside `[0.648, 1]`; the printed range `[0.60, 1.25]` contains the result.
declarations.name: stepE_lambda_0_range

declarations.doc: The interpolant coefficient scales exactly with the anchor it is built from: replacing `1215/1024` by `1095/1024` sends `b = -405/176` to `b' = -365/176`.
declarations.name: stepE_b_scales_with_anchor

declarations.doc: `S <= max(60 lambda_0', lambda_0', |w| P^(-1/2)) <= 65 P^(-1/2)` under (C1) `k h1 h2 <= P^(1/8)` and `|w| <= 2`; the paper prints the rounder `80`.
declarations.name: stepE_S_bound

declarations.doc: The `j = 0` middle band takes `V = (1/12) S^(1/2) P^(-11/24)` at `S >= 0.60 P^(-5/8)`, so `V >= 0.064 P^(-37/48)` -- and **not** `0.065`, which the draft printed. Squaring avoids the square root.
declarations.name: stepE_j0_V_constant

declarations.doc: Lemma 6.2's exponent bookkeeping: `m^(9/8)` at `X = n^(3/2)` is `n^(27/16)` with sawtooth coefficient exponent `3/16`, and `v^(1/4)` is `n^(9/16)`.
declarations.name: lemma62_exponents

declarations.doc: The residual `theta`-coefficient after the window expansion: `27k/32 - 9k/16 = 9k/32`, so one slow sawtooth survives.
declarations.name: oeoe_C_net

declarations.doc: Its window-centre `X`-mode has curvature `(9/32)(3/4) = 27/128 = 216/1024`.
declarations.name: oeoe_window_curvature

declarations.doc: The leading `n^(27/16)` coefficient of the combined phase is `k/2 - 3k/4`.
declarations.name: oeoe_leading_coefficient

declarations.doc: Its curvature is `-(1/4)(27/16)(11/16) = -297/1024`, the exponent dropping from `27/16` to `-5/16`.
declarations.name: oeoe_leading_curvature

declarations.doc: The composite does not vanish: `-297/1024 + 216/1024 = -81/1024 <> 0`. This is what makes the curvature single-signed, hence Lemma 3.3 applicable.
declarations.name: oeoe_composite_nonzero

declarations.doc: The balance `J^(1/2) P^(27/32) = P/J` is struck at `J = P^(5/48)` and gives `P^(43/48)`.
declarations.name: oeoe_balance

declarations.doc: Corollary 6.4: the five disjoint certificate classes `E`, `OE`, `OOEE`, `OOOEE`, `OOEOE` have densities summing to `7/8`.
declarations.name: cor64_density

declarations.doc: The error is the worse of the two fifth-letter exponents, and `1 - 1/96` is the worse of them.
declarations.name: cor64_error_exponent

declarations.doc: **Step B's discard.** With `|err| <= (3/4) n^(-9/8)` in the phase `(k/2) v^(3/2)`, a block costs `2 pi (k/2)(3/4) P^(-9/8) * P = (3 pi k/4) P^(-1/8)`, which at `k <= 2 P^(1/96)` is under one unit as soon as `4.72 P^(-11/96) <= 1`. In `P = t^96` that is `4.72 <= t^11`, which holds from `t >= 1.16`. An earlier draft printed this cost as `<= 7 P^(7/8)`, which multiplied by the block length twice and additionally needed `k <= 7/(2 pi) = 1.11`.
declarations.name: stepB_discard

declarations.doc: **Paid for.** The Stage 5 collision-band sum is `3 R_0^(1/2) P^(3/4)`, which must stay inside the theorem's own `P^(23/24)`. At `a = 5/16` that is `3 P^(29/32) <= P^(23/24)`, i.e. `3 <= P^(5/96) = t^5`, from `t >= 1.25` (`P >= 2.0e9`).
declarations.name: row_st2_collision

declarations.doc: **Paid for.** The `q''` curvature of Step 5b(a) is `(1.85 k h P^(1/8) + R_0) * 3|j| P^(-5/4)`, whose ratio to the main curvature `0.35 P^(-3/4)` must clear the margin `1/4`. In `t` that is `126.86 t^28 + 68.57 t^30 <= t^48`; dividing by `t^28` gives the form below, which holds from `t >= 1.32` (`P >= 3.8e11`, still two and a half orders under `P_0`).
declarations.name: row_st5b_qpp

declarations.doc: **Bought.** Theorem 6.3's fifth-letter Lemma 3.7 window is opened at `T = R_0` against `|C| <= (9/8) 2^(3/16) P^(19/96)`, and its hypothesis `T >= 8(1 + |C|)` reads `8 + 10.25 t^19 <= t^30` at `a = 5/16`, since `8 * (9/8) * 2^(3/16) = 10.2491 <= 10.25`. It holds from `t >= 1.24` (`P >= 9.3e8`).
declarations.name: row_t63_window

declarations.doc: **Bought, and this is the one that binds.** The same window's *flat cost* is `8(1 + |C|)/T` per point, which over a block must stay inside `P^(1-1/96)`. That reads `8 t + 10.25 t^20 <= t^30`, holding from `t >= 1.27` (`P >= 9.2e9`). At `a = 1/4` the same line is `8 t + 10.25 t^20 <= t^24`, which does not hold until `1.8e24` --- ten orders above `P_0`, and the real reason Stage 2 is run at `P^(5/16)`.
declarations.name: row_t63_flat

declarations.doc: The superseded truncation `a = 1/4` really does fail, and it fails at `P_0`. There `t = P_0^(1/96) <= 1.4`, so `t^5 <= 5.38` and `t^24 = t^19 * t^5` cannot reach `10.25 t^19`, let alone `8 + 10.25 t^19`. This is the window hypothesis at `T = P^(1/4)`; the flat cost at that truncation fails by ten orders more.
declarations.name: row_t63_window_fails_at_quarter

declarations.doc: **Claim D of Lemma 5.2(ii) → (i).** Every index of the Claim C sum must be a legal shift for part (i), i.e. `h_3 <= P^(1/8)`, from `h_3 <= t^(1/3) P^(1/12)`. The exponent gap is `1/8 - 7/72 = 1/36`, so whatever constant stands in front of `P^(7/72)` is paid at the thirty-sixth power, and which bound on `t` is carried decides the row entirely: * the individual `|q_d| <= 4 P^(1/24)` over the four elements of `D` gives `|t| <= 16 P^(1/24)`, hence `16^(1/3) < 2.52` and a threshold `16^12 = 2.8e14` --- which would be the binding row of the whole paper; * the total frequency bound `|t| <= 3 P^(1/24)`, which Theorem 5.3 Step 4 (the only place (ii) is invoked) supplies because the wave modes arrive one per expansion layer from three layers at truncation `J_2 = P^(1/24)`, gives `3^(1/3) < 1.45` and a threshold `3^12 = 5.3e5`. Lemma 5.2(ii) carries the second as a hypothesis. In `P = t^72` the two exponents become `7` and `9`, so the requirement is `1.45 <= t^2`, holding from `t >= 1.205` (`P >= 6.8e5`).
declarations.name: claimD_shift_range

declarations.doc: The loose bound really would have cost a factor 3.15 in `P_0`: with `2.52` in front, the comparison fails at `P_0 = 8.95e13`, where `t = P_0^(1/72) <= 1.58` and `t^2 <= 2.4964 < 2.52`.
declarations.name: claimD_loose_bound_fails_at_P0

declarations.doc: Step 3(a)'s flat cost is `23 P^(19/24)`, which sits inside the Step 6 budget `P^(23/24)` from `23^6 = 1.5e8`, but **not** inside `P^(7/8)`, which an earlier draft printed and which would need `23^12 = 2.2e16`. In `P = t^24`: `23 t^19 <= t^23`.
declarations.name: st3a_flat_cost

declarations.doc: Even `n` maps to `Nat.sqrt n`; odd `n` maps to `Nat.sqrt (n^3)`.
declarations.name: floorPower

declarations.doc: Integer obstruction: `k^4 ≤ n^3` and `n ≥ 2` forbid `k ≥ n`. This is iterated `Nat.sqrt` of `n^3`, not `T^2` on the odd-to-odd branch.
declarations.name: sqrt_sqrt_n_cubed_lt

declarations.doc: On the odd-to-even branch, `T^2(n) < n`. Not a halt theorem for the full map.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_even_two_step_lt

declarations.doc: Integer comparison: `(n+1)^2 ≤ n^3` for `n ≥ 3`. Threshold for odd-branch growth.
declarations.name: succ_sq_le_cube

declarations.doc: On the odd branch, `n ≥ 3` implies `T(n) > n`. Independent of the parity of `T(n)`.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_gt

declarations.doc: The odd branch is nondecreasing: `k ≤ T(k)` when `k` is odd and positive.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_nondecreasing

declarations.doc: On the odd-to-odd branch with `n ≥ 3`, `T^2(n) > n`. Dual of `floorPower_odd_even_two_step_lt`. Not a divergence theorem.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_odd_two_step_gt

declarations.doc: Combined odd-state two-step direction for `n ≥ 3`. Not a macro-transition law, not a halt theorem, and not a divergence theorem. The case `n = 1` is excluded: `floorPower 1 = 1`.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_macro_direction

declarations.doc: Even branch: `T(n)^2 ≤ n`. Exact floor bound, not a real square root.
declarations.name: floorPower_even_sq_le

declarations.doc: Odd branch: `T(n)^2 ≤ n^3`. Exact floor bound, not a real 3/2-power.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_sq_le_cube

declarations.doc: Odd squares attain the one-step envelope: odd `m` implies `T(m^2)^2 = (m^2)^3`.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_sq_eq_cube_of_sq

declarations.doc: Smallest mixed-equality witness: word `O` at `n=9`.
declarations.name: floorPower_nine_odd_eq

declarations.doc: Packet seed: `T(13) = 46`.
declarations.name: floorPower_thirteen_step

declarations.doc: Named expansion of the OOOEE envelope `n5 ^ 32 ≤ n ^ 27`.
declarations.name: floorPower_oooee_pow_chain

declarations.doc: Even-step composition of a square upper bound.
declarations.name: pow_sq_le

declarations.doc: Odd-step composition of a square-vs-cube upper bound.
declarations.name: pow_sq_le_cube

declarations.doc: For `n ≥ 2`, a strictly larger exponent yields a strictly larger power.
declarations.name: pow_lt_of_two_le

declarations.doc: Weak one-sided bound `m^{2^k} ≤ n^{3^o}`. Equality is allowed.
declarations.name: PowerBound

declarations.doc: Free-exponent envelope `x^A ≤ n^B`. `PowerBound` is the special case `A = 2^k`, `B = 3^o`. Word algebra only.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState

declarations.doc: Even letter: `(A, B) → (2A, B)` from `T(x)^2 ≤ x`.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState.even

declarations.doc: Odd letter: `(A, B) → (2A, 3B)` from `T(x)^2 ≤ x^3`.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState.odd

declarations.doc: Empty-itinerary envelope: `n^1 ≤ n^1`.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState.refl

declarations.doc: One realized letter.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState.map_letter

declarations.doc: Compose an envelope along a realized itinerary.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState.map_itinerary

declarations.doc: Word envelope from `map_itinerary` on `refl`.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState.of_follows

declarations.doc: Weak composition: every realized finite itinerary obeys the one-sided bound.
declarations.name: power_bound_follows

declarations.doc: Unfolded form of `power_bound_follows`. Naming alias only.
declarations.name: power_bound_word

declarations.doc: Repeated realized `OE` blocks: `T^{2r}(x)^{4^r} ≤ x^{3^r}`.
declarations.name: repeated_oe_scale

declarations.doc: Cell comparison: `x^A ≤ n^B` and `B < k·A` force `x < n^k`.
declarations.name: envelope_lt_pow

declarations.doc: Word-stat form: `3^{oddCount w} < k · 2^{|w|}` yields `T_w(n) < n^k`. Implemented by `EnvelopeState.of_follows`. `power_bound_contracts` is the `k = 1` case.
declarations.name: power_bound_lt_pow

declarations.doc: Strict block contraction from the exponent gap. Domain `n ≥ 2`. The `k = 1` case of `power_bound_lt_pow`. Not a claim that every trajectory meets a negative-drift word.
declarations.name: power_bound_contracts

declarations.doc: On the OOOEE branch itinerary, `T^5(n) < n` for `n ≥ 2`. Wrapper of `floorPower_oooee_of_follows`. Not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: floorPower_oooee_five_step_lt

declarations.doc: Power comparison for the OOOEEEOO floor-power block: five odd steps and three even steps give `n8 ^ 256 ≤ n ^ 243`. Canonical exponents of the itinerary exponent `243/256`.
declarations.name: floorPower_oooeeeoo_pow_chain

declarations.doc: On the OOOEEEOO branch itinerary, `T^8(n) < n` for `n ≥ 2`. Wrapper of `floorPower_oooeeeoo_of_follows`. Not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: floorPower_oooeeeoo_eight_step_lt

declarations.doc: An all-even realized itinerary of length `k ≥ 1` contracts for `n ≥ 2`.
declarations.name: even_itinerary_contracts

declarations.doc: Even-run envelope: `T^r(m)^{2^r} ≤ m`. No minimality.
declarations.name: even_run_pow_le

declarations.doc: An all-odd realized itinerary of length `k ≥ 1` expands for `n ≥ 3`.
declarations.name: odd_itinerary_expands

declarations.doc: A realized return to `x ≥ 2` forces `2^r ≤ 3^o`.
declarations.name: cycle_envelope

declarations.doc: Equality `2^r = 3^o` is impossible for a nonempty itinerary, so every nontrivial cycle is strictly expanding in the exponent.
declarations.name: cycle_strict_envelope

declarations.doc: Contracting words cannot close a cycle.
declarations.name: cycle_not_contracting

declarations.doc: Even branch: `T(n)^2 = n` iff `n` is a perfect square.
declarations.name: floorPower_even_sq_eq_iff_square

declarations.doc: Odd branch: `T(n)^2 = n^3` iff `n` is a perfect square.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_sq_eq_cube_iff_square

declarations.doc: Equality form of the one-sided envelope. Independent of `PowerBound`.
declarations.name: PowerBoundEq

declarations.doc: Even append: composite equality forces the previous equality and local tightness.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_of_append_even

declarations.doc: Odd append: composite equality forces the previous equality and local tightness.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_of_append_odd

declarations.doc: Local tightness of one realized letter.
declarations.name: localTight

declarations.doc: Every local branch inequality along a realized itinerary is tight.
declarations.name: localsTight

declarations.doc: Global envelope equality forces every local branch inequality to be tight.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_implies_local_eq

declarations.doc: Global envelope equality forces every relevant itinerary state to be a square.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_implies_square

declarations.doc: Even square: the even branch is exact as an image, not only as a power.
declarations.name: floorPower_of_even_sq

declarations.doc: Odd square: the odd branch maps `s^2` to `s^3`.
declarations.name: floorPower_of_odd_sq

declarations.doc: Exact even branch on a `2^r`-th power, `r ≥ 1`.
declarations.name: floorPower_of_pow_two_depth_even

declarations.doc: Exact odd branch on a `2^r`-th power, `r ≥ 1`.
declarations.name: floorPower_of_pow_two_depth_odd

declarations.doc: A cube that is a `2^m`-th power is the cube of a `2^m`-th power's base.
declarations.name: hasPowTwoDepth_of_cube

declarations.doc: Even exact step drops 2-adic depth by one.
declarations.name: hasPowTwoDepth_even_exact

declarations.doc: Odd exact step drops 2-adic depth by one (`a^{3·2^{r-1}} = (a^3)^{2^{r-1}}`).
declarations.name: hasPowTwoDepth_odd_exact

declarations.doc: Depth at least 2 forces the exact image to remain a square.
declarations.name: hasPowTwoDepth_ge_two_image_square

declarations.doc: Depth exactly one: the exact image need not be a square.
declarations.name: hasPowTwoDepth_one_image_sq_iff

declarations.doc: Envelope equality of length `k` forces the start to be a `2^k`-th power.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_implies_pow_two_depth

declarations.doc: A contracting equality itinerary of length `k` at `n ≥ 2` is at least `2^{2^k}`.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_contracts_pow_two_lb

declarations.doc: An exact step on a square keeps the parity of the state.
declarations.name: floorPower_sq_preserves_parity

declarations.doc: Exact even or odd branch on `a^{2^r}` keeps the parity of `a`.
declarations.name: floorPower_pow_two_depth_preserves_parity

declarations.doc: Envelope equality forces a monochrome word.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_implies_monochrome

declarations.doc: Equality saturates iff the itinerary is an exact even or odd tower.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_iff_extremal

declarations.doc: Among \(n\ge 3\), an all-odd equality of length `k` is at least `3^{2^k}`.
declarations.name: odd_equality_three_pow_le

declarations.doc: A uniformly bounded trajectory repeats. Finite pigeonhole on the prefix of length `M + 2`.
declarations.name: bounded_trajectory_eventually_cycles

declarations.doc: No nontrivial cycle implies no bounded nontermination. This is not a no-cycle theorem and not a halt theorem: unbounded escape remains.
declarations.name: no_nontrivial_cycle_no_bounded_nonterm

declarations.doc: Same square-cell comparison as the human `OOEOOE` corridor, with no `CycleMin` return hypothesis.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooe_image_lt_sq

declarations.doc: The itinerary `OOEOOEO` has the square-cell gap `256 > 243`.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooeo_image_lt_sq

declarations.doc: Even `OOEOOE` landing is the shared square trap, hence `FiniteProgress`. No cycle-return hypothesis.
declarations.name: finiteProgress_of_ooeooe_even_landing

declarations.doc: Even `OOEOOE` landing is descent, hence impossible on a CE.
declarations.name: minimal_ooeooe_not_even_landing

declarations.doc: On a CE, `OOEOOE` forces another `OO`. The next completed letter after the forced `O` cannot be `E`.
declarations.name: minimal_ooeooe_forces_oo

declarations.doc: A CE never realizes a formally contracting itinerary. Contrapositive of `power_bound_contracts`.
declarations.name: minimal_nonterm_not_exponentGap

declarations.doc: Every realized prefix of a CE is prefix-noncontracting. Concatenating expanding residual blocks therefore cannot create an exponent certificate on a CE. This is not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: minimal_nonterm_prefix_noncontracting

declarations.doc: The itinerary `OOEOOEOO` has the cube-cell gap `768 > 729`.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooeoo_image_lt_cube

declarations.doc: The completed third `OOE` has the square-cell gap `1024 > 729`.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooeooe_image_lt_sq

declarations.doc: On a CE, a completed third `OOE` cannot land even: the landing is below `n^2`, so an even landing is descent. This is not a PE theorem.
declarations.name: minimal_ooeooeooe_not_even_landing

declarations.doc: The escaped-even `OE` after a third `OOE` has the square-cell gap `4096 > 2187`. This is not a length-11 cycle census.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooeooeoe_image_lt_sq

declarations.doc: On a CE, the `OE` landing after a third `OOE` cannot be even. The landing is below `n^2`, so an even landing is descent. This does not kill an odd landing such as `1517`.
declarations.name: minimal_ooeooeooeoe_not_even_landing

declarations.doc: After an odd `OE` landing the next `O` still has the square-cell gap `8192 > 6561`. Another escaped even is impossible on this step.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooeooeoeo_image_lt_sq

declarations.doc: On a CE, the next image after an odd `OE` landing is odd and below `n^2`. An even image would be descent. This is not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: minimal_ooeooeooeoeo_not_even

declarations.doc: The second `O` after the new `OO` loses the square cell (`19683 > 16384`) but keeps the cube-cell gap `24576 > 19683`. The square comparison `3^9 < 2 · 2^13` fails; see `ooeooeooeoeoo_loses_square`. A cube-cell even landing is therefore not `FiniteProgress`.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooeooeoeoo_image_lt_cube

declarations.doc: Trailing odd-run of any itinerary: the prefix is empty or ends even.
declarations.name: exists_trailing_odds

declarations.doc: A CycleMin itinerary cannot end `O^a E` for `a ≥ 2`. This is `no_cycleMin_odd_run` when the prefix is empty and `no_cycleMin_bootstrap_last_gap` after an internal even.
declarations.name: cycleMin_not_last_odd_run_ge_two

declarations.doc: On a CycleMin itinerary ending `O^a E` with `a ≥ 1` and the preceding letter not odd, the last odd-run has length exactly one. Paper A §3 writes that last excursion as unconstrained `O^{a_e}E`; this is the `OOEOOE` sandwich of Theorem 3.6 at an arbitrary last valley.
declarations.name: cycleMin_last_odd_run_eq_one

declarations.doc: Every CycleMin itinerary ends `O^a E` with `a ≤ 1`. The case `a = 0` is a trailing even run of length at least two.
declarations.name: exists_cycleMin_last_odd_run

declarations.doc: **Even-count assembler.** No `n ≥ 2` realizes a cycle itinerary with at most three even letters. This is not a length census and not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: no_cycle_itinerary_even_count_le_three

declarations.doc: A nontrivial cycle itinerary has length at least eleven: four evens plus the expansion demand \(2^{|w|}<3^{\#O}\).
declarations.name: cycle_itinerary_length_ge_eleven

declarations.doc: Return on the first `O^a E` is an even-count-1 cycle itinerary.
declarations.name: no_cycle_itinerary_oddEvenBlock_one

declarations.doc: On a `MinimalNonTerm` start the first even residual always overshoots. The return cell is an even-count-1 cycle itinerary. This is not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: minimal_first_even_overshoots

declarations.doc: On a `CycleMin` the first even residual overshoots. Return would be an even-count-1 cycle itinerary.
declarations.name: cycleMin_first_even_overshoots

declarations.doc: Every `CycleMin` itinerary is a first-even block plus a nonempty tail.
declarations.name: cycleMin_exists_oddEven_split

declarations.doc: On a cycle minimum the maximum sits at or above `(n+1)^2`. The first even residual already overshoots, so the first-cell family `n^2 < M < (n+1)^2` is impossible. Not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: cycleMin_max_ge_succ_sq

declarations.doc: On a cycle maximum the rotated minimum satisfies `(m+1)^2 ≤ M`.
declarations.name: cycleMax_min_succ_sq_le

declarations.doc: The maximum cannot collapse to the minimum in one even step.
declarations.name: cycleMax_landing_gt_min

declarations.doc: Laboratory sharpening of `cycle_distinguished_order`: first-even overshoot replaces `m^2 < M` by `(m+1)^2 ≤ M`.
declarations.name: cycle_distinguished_order_succ_sq

declarations.doc: Formal expansion of an `O^a E^b` block is an odd-density bound.
declarations.name: expanding_implies_odd_density

declarations.doc: Largest even-run length compatible with formal expansion.
declarations.name: maxExpandingEvens

declarations.doc: For `a ≥ 1`, `O^a E^b` expands if and only if `a+b ≤ log₂(3^a)`.
declarations.name: expanding_oddEvenBlock_iff_log

declarations.doc: Persistence is already expansion: a contracting residual cannot overshoot `n ≥ 2`.
declarations.name: persistent_odd_residual_expanding

declarations.doc: **The closed form.** With `a = √v` and `b = √Y` (so `θ₂ = b² - a²` is the level-2 defect `Y - v`), the Taylor defect `Y^(3/2) - v^(3/2) - (3/2)v^(1/2)θ₂` is exactly `½(b-a)²(2b+a)`. Since `Y^(3/2) = m^(9/4)`, the manuscript's remainder is `R = ¼(b-a)²(2b+a)`.
declarations.name: lemma51_i_closed_form

declarations.doc: **`0 ≤ R`.** The level-2 defect remainder is one-signed, as the manuscript needs.
declarations.name: lemma51_i_nonneg

declarations.doc: **`R·a ≤ (3/16)θ₂²`**, i.e. `R ≤ (3/16)θ₂²v^(-1/2)`; at `θ₂ < 1` this is the printed `R ≤ (3/16)v^(-1/2)`. Reduces to `(a + 3b)(a - b) ≤ 0`.
declarations.name: lemma51_i_upper

declarations.doc: The manuscript's form: `(3/4)v^(1/2)θ₂ = ½(m^(9/4) - v^(3/2)) - R`, stated with `v = a²`, `Y = b²`, `m^(9/4) = Y^(3/2) = b³`.
declarations.name: lemma51_i_identity

declarations.doc: **The sawtooth form of the carry**, the elementary identity the manuscript displays: `[{A}+{B} ≥ 1] = {A} + {B} - {A+B}`. Both sides equal `{A}+{B}-{A+B}` because `{A}+{B} ∈ [0,2)`.
declarations.name: carry_as_sawtooth

declarations.doc: **The substitution engine.** One step of the level-2 bookkeeping: the increment of the defect `θ₂ = {Y}` across a shift equals the sawtooth of the gap minus the carry. Every substitution in Lemma 5.1(iv) is this lemma.
declarations.name: fract_diff_level2

declarations.doc: **Lemma 5.1(ii), the double gap.** With `v = ⌊Y⌋`, `g₂ = Δ₁v`, `W = Δ₁Y` and `ΔΔY = Δ₂W`, the second difference of the integer part is `Δ₂g₂ = ⌊ΔΔY⌋ + κ'' + Δ₂κ₂` — two applications of the carry identity, first to `Y` at shift `d₁`, then to `W` at shift `d₂`.
declarations.name: lemma51_double_gap

declarations.doc: **The product rule over four base points.** With `ΔΔg = g₁₂ - g₁ - g₂ + g₀`, `(Δ₂c)(n+d₁) = c₁₂ - c₁` and `(Δ₁c)(n+d₂) = c₁₂ - c₂`, `ΔΔ(cf) = c₁₁·ΔΔf + (Δ₂c)(n+d₁)·Δ₁f + (Δ₁c)(n+d₂)·Δ₂f + (ΔΔc)·f`. The manuscript says "verified by expanding both sides over the four base points"; that expansion is `ring`.
declarations.name: double_difference_product

declarations.doc: **Lemma 5.1(iv), the master identity.** The doubly differenced kernel phase `ΔΔ(c·θ₂)`, with `θ₂ = {Y}` the level-2 defect, decomposes exactly into four terms, in each of which the non-smooth factor is a *bounded* bracket: * `(ΔΔc)·θ₂`, with `θ₂ ∈ [0,1)`; * `(Δ₂c)(n+d₁)·({W} - κ₂)`, with `W = Δ₁Y` and `κ₂` the level-2 carry; * `(Δ₁c)(n+d₂)·({W'} - κ₂')`, with `W' = Δ₂Y`; * `c₁₁·({ΔΔY} - κ'' - Δ₂κ₂)`. No unbounded smooth part survives the differencing — which is the whole purpose of the lemma. The proof is the product rule of Section 3 together with three applications of `fract_diff_level2`.
declarations.name: lemma51_master

declarations.doc: **Every bracket is bounded by `2`.** This is what the decomposition buys: the three carry brackets and the defect itself are all `O(1)`, so the doubly differenced phase carries no growing amplitude.
declarations.name: lemma51_brackets_le_two

declarations.doc: `(x^(3/2))' = (3/2)x^(1/2)`, from `Real.hasDerivAt_sqrt`.
declarations.name: hasDerivAt_pow32

declarations.doc: **The first mean value theorem, made explicit.** In root coordinates `a = √A`, `b = √(A+j)`, the increment of `x^(3/2)` is `(3/2)(b² - a²)·c` with `c = (2/3)(a² + ab + b²)/(a + b)`, and `a ≤ c ≤ b`. So `ξ₁ = c² - A` lies between `0` and `j`, exactly as the manuscript needs — with no appeal to the mean value theorem.
declarations.name: mvt_cube_explicit

declarations.doc: **The inner mean value, made explicit.** For `F' = (3/2)x^(1/2)` and `F'' = (3/4)x^(-1/2)`, the increment `F'(A+B) - F'(A)` equals `B·F''(η)` *exactly*, with `√η` the **arithmetic mean** of `√A` and `√(A+B)`. Written in root coordinates `a = √A`, `b = √(A+B)`: `(3/2)(b - a) = (b² - a²)·(3/4)/((a+b)/2)`, and `(a+b)/2 ∈ [a, b]`.
declarations.name: mvt_sqrt_diff_explicit

declarations.doc: **The second difference is `β₁β₂ F''(m + ξ₂)`**, in the two-sided form the manuscript uses. One mean value theorem for `gShift`, then the explicit inner witness and the monotonicity of `√`: `(3/4)β₁β₂ (m+β₁+β₂)^(-1/2) ≤ D ≤ (3/4)β₁β₂ m^(-1/2)`.
declarations.name: second_difference_two_sided

declarations.doc: **The manuscript's own form of the second mean value.** There is a genuine `ξ₂ ∈ [m, m+β₁+β₂]` with `D = β₁β₂ F''(ξ₂)`, `F'' = (3/4)x^(-1/2)`. The witness is `√ξ₂ = (3/4)β₁β₂/D`, and the two-sided bound above is exactly what places it in range.
declarations.name: second_difference_exists_xi

declarations.doc: **Lemma 5.1(iii) is now unconditional.** The two mean values the manuscript appeals to are supplied: the first explicitly (`mvt_cube_explicit`), the second through one application of the mean value theorem plus the explicit inner witness (`second_difference_two_sided`). Nothing in Lemma 5.1 is now assumed beyond the definitions.
declarations.name: lemma51iii_mean_values_available

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3.9, Step-5b triple.** For `(α, β, γ) = (5/4, 11/8, 3/2)` the exponents `x = α - 2` are `-3/4, -5/8, -1/2`, and the system `u = A + B + C`, `v = Σ xᵢ Aᵢ`, `w = Σ xᵢ(xᵢ - 1) Aᵢ` inverts to the integer matrix printed in the note.
declarations.name: step5b_curvature_inverse

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3.9, the constant `c₇`.** The `ℓ^∞` operator norm of the inverse is the maximal absolute row sum, `max(110, 232, 123) = 232`, so at every point one of the three derivative orders is at least `1/232` of the largest curvature term.
declarations.name: step5b_curvature_norm

declarations.doc: The manuscript's Step 5b quotes the weaker `c₇ = 1/288`; it follows from `step5b_curvature_norm` since `232 ≤ 288`.

declarations.doc: Soundness of the vector form: bounds on the three tests transfer to the three curvature terms through `|M⁻¹|`. This is `step5b_curvature_inverse` read with the triangle inequality.

declarations.doc: The uniform choice `c₂ = c₃ = c₄ = 1/232` saturates the middle row exactly: `24 + 144 + 64 = 232`. So there is no free improvement --- any increase in `c₂` must be paid for out of `c₃` and `c₄`.
declarations.name: step5b_uniform_saturates

declarations.doc: The ceiling on `c₂`. Feasibility of the middle row alone, with `c₃, c₄ ≥ 0`, gives `c₂ ≤ 1/24`: at most a factor `232/24 < 10` is available, and only in the limit `c₃, c₄ → 0`.
declarations.name: step5b_c2_ceiling

declarations.doc: The operating point that minimises the threshold `P₀` alone: `c = (1/27, 1/1872, 1/1872)` is feasible, and again exactly tight on the middle row (`8/9 + 1/9 = 1`).
declarations.name: step5b_c2_optimum_feasible

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3.8, the constant `c₆`.** With `p = α - 2`, `q = β - 2` the lemma needs `min_{s>0} max(|1 - s|, |p - q s|) > 0`. Over the ordered pairs of `E` the minimum is `1/14`, attained at `(α, β) = (11/8, 5/4)`, where `p = -5/8`, `q = -3/4`; the two V-shapes cross at `s = 13/14`.

declarations.doc: The value `1/14` is attained, so `c₆ = 1/14` is sharp for this pair and `ρ₀(E) ≤ c₆/8 = 1/112` is the admissible perturbation size.
declarations.name: c6_eleven_eighths_five_fourths_attained

declarations.doc: Upper side of the sandwich: `3^10781274 < 2^17087915`, hence `log 2 / log 3 > 10781274 / 17087915`. Proved by `norm_num`, so the comparison is checked by the kernel rather than by the compiled runtime: these two inequalities carry the whole Ostrowski certification, and `Nat` literal arithmetic is GMP-backed in the kernel, so the five-million-digit comparison costs well under a second. Only the exponent threshold is raised, and only for this declaration: it gates whether the power is evaluated at all, whereas `maxRecDepth` is not consulted on this route.
declarations.name: theta_sandwich_upper

declarations.doc: Lower side of the sandwich: `2^16785921 < 3^10590737`, hence `log 2 / log 3 < 10590737 / 16785921`. Kernel-checked, as above.

declarations.doc: **The closed form.** With `a = √m` and `b = √X = n^(3/4)`, the remainder `E = m^(3/2) - (3/2)mX^(1/2) + (1/2)X^(3/2)` of Lemma 4.3(i) equals `½(a-b)²(2a+b)` identically. The manuscript obtains only `E = (3/8)(X-ξ)^(-1/2)θ²` for an unspecified mean value `ξ`.
declarations.name: lemma43_closed_form

declarations.doc: **`0 ≤ E`**, the lower bound of Lemma 4.3(i): the remainder is one-signed. This is what lets the manuscript treat `E` as a nonnegative error throughout.
declarations.name: lemma43_nonneg

declarations.doc: The bridge to the manuscript's variables: `m = a²`, `X = b²`, `a = √m`, `b = √X`. Then `m^(3/2) = m·a` and `X^(3/2) = X·b`.
declarations.name: lemma43_remainder_sqrt

declarations.doc: Instantiated at the actual square roots.
declarations.name: lemma43_remainder_of_sqrt

declarations.doc: **Lemma 4.3(ii).** For the level-1 wave `x = n^(3/2)` and the smooth gap `δ`, the integer gap `⌊x + δ⌋ - ⌊x⌋` is `⌊δ⌋` plus a carry which is `1` exactly when `{x} + {δ} ≥ 1`. This is the identity behind `G = ⌊δ⌋ + κ`, `κ ∈ {0,1}`, and hence behind `|G - δ| ≤ 1` in Lemma 5.2b step (i).
declarations.name: carry_identity

declarations.doc: The carry is `0` or `1` — the form used in Lemma 5.2b.
declarations.name: carry_mem_zero_one

declarations.doc: **Step (i) of Lemma 5.2b.** The wave replacement, under the middle-band cap `u ≤ 300 k h₂ P^(1/8)` — which *is* the band condition `μ ≤ 60 λ₀`, since `60·4.2/0.84 = 300`. Powers enter only through `p18 = P^(1/8)`, `p54 = P^(-5/4)`, `p98 = P^(-9/8)` and the relation `p18 · p54 = p98`. The conclusion carries the shape `k(h₁+h₂)`, which is what lets it combine with step (ii) *before* conversion — the step the earlier draft skipped, bounding and converting the two terms separately and printing `202.5 + 16 = 219`. The constant is `(9/32)·300 = 84.375`, printed as `84.38`. The cap is `300` and not `186` because of the erratum at Lemma 5.2b: the anchor curvature is `27/128`, not `135/1024`, and `λ₀`'s ceiling `2.6` opens to `4.2`. The superseded chain is kept below under `_precorrection`, as `step5b_c7_printed` keeps the manuscript's weaker `1/288`.
declarations.name: interpolant_step_i

declarations.doc: The same step under the pre-correction anchor `135/1024`, where the cap was `186 = 60·2.6/0.84` and the constant `(9/32)·186 = 52.3125`. Retained because the manuscript's erratum lists `186 → 300` and `52.9 → 85.3` explicitly, and a reader checking that list should find both ends of it here.
declarations.name: interpolant_step_i_precorrection

declarations.doc: **Step (ii) of Lemma 5.2b.** The `β`-product replacement contributes `(27/128)·4.3 = 0.9070`, printed as `0.91`. The manuscript notes that `0.95` would not do, because it pushes the sum in (i) past `85.3`; both halves of that are recorded here.
declarations.name: interpolant_step_ii_constant

declarations.doc: The same constant under the pre-correction anchor, `(135/1024)·4.3 = 0.567`, printed as `0.57`; the erratum's factor is exactly `8/5`. An earlier draft carried `8` here — fourteen times the pre-correction value — and that `8` is the source of the `16` in the old `219 = 202.5 + 16`.
declarations.name: interpolant_step_ii_precorrection

declarations.doc: **The assembly.** Steps (i) and (ii) share the shape `k(h₁+h₂)P^(-9/8)`, so they add before conversion: `84.38 + 0.91 = 85.29`. Then `k(h₁+h₂) ≤ 2 P^(1/12)` by (C3),(C4) gives `170.58 ≤ 170.6`, with `p112 = P^(1/12)`, `p2524 = P^(-25/24)` and `p112 · p98 = p2524`. The manuscript prints the rounder `171`; `170.6` is what `p0_certificate.interpolant_error` uses and is what the nine anchor rows of the threshold certificate are solved against.
declarations.name: interpolant_assembly

declarations.doc: The same assembly under the pre-correction anchor: `52.32 + 0.57 = 52.89` and `105.78 ≤ 106`.
declarations.name: interpolant_assembly_precorrection

declarations.doc: The gain over the earlier `219`, on the `P^(-25/24)` coefficient: `1.28`, which is what Appendix A.5 claims. The pre-correction chain gave `106` and so a factor above `2`; the erratum at Lemma 5.2b spends most of that back, and `1.28` is what is left. The second term `0.11 P^(-5/6)` of the interpolant error is untouched and is co-dominant at `P₀`, so the *total* error gains less than either figure there.
declarations.name: interpolant_gain

declarations.doc: **The differenced (D3) budget is dominated**, at margin 4 and better: `6 K h P^(-13/8) ≤ ¼ · 0.35 u h P^(-3/4)` reduces, after multiplying by `p^39`, to `6K ≤ 0.0875 u p^21`, which holds by `K ≤ p^3` and `u ≥ 1`.
declarations.name: stage6_D3_differenced_dominated

declarations.doc: **The undifferenced budget is not dominated.** At the (C1) extreme `K = p^3` and `u = h = 1`, the ratio of `3 K P^(-5/8)` to the Stage-4 curvature `0.35 u h P^(-3/4)` is `(3/0.35) p^6 = 8.57 P^(1/4)` -- it exceeds the curvature by an unbounded factor, so Lemma 3.3 at that scale does not apply and the two can cancel outright.
declarations.name: stage6_D3_printed_not_dominated

declarations.doc: **The size of the gap.** The undifferenced budget exceeds the differenced one by exactly `P/(2h) = p^24/(2h)`; at `h ≤ P^(1/8)` that is at least `½P^(7/8)`.
declarations.name: stage6_D3_gap

declarations.doc: **Regime A: the undifferenced budget is dominated.** `3 K P^(-5/8) ≤ ¼·0.35 u h P^(-3/4)` holds as soon as `u h ≥ (12/0.35) K P^(1/8)`, and `12/0.35 = 34.28…`. Written at `P = p^24`, after multiplying by `p^15`.
declarations.name: wideD3_regimeA_dominated

declarations.doc: **Regime B is a small-`uh` regime.** By (C1), `K ≤ p^3`, so regime B forces `u h < 34.3 p^3 = 34.3 P^(1/8)`… and with `u h ≤ P^(1/2)` from the hypotheses of (i) this is the range where the Stage-4 curvature is weakest.
declarations.name: wideD3_regimeB_small

declarations.doc: **The frozen `G` steps by one, so `f'` jumps at every cell boundary.** The jump is `(9/8) u (ν+2h)^(-1/4)`; the point is only that it is *bounded below*, which no choice of the continuous decoration can affect. Over `N` cells the total sweep of `f'` is at least `N` times that.
declarations.name: wideD3_frequency_sweep

declarations.doc: **The cells are flat in regime B.** At the sawtooth curvature scale `0.282 u P^(-5/4)`, over a cell of length `ℓ ≤ 0.95 P^(1/2)/h` the phase departs from linear by `≤ 0.282 u P^(-5/4) ℓ² ≤ 0.26 u P^(-1/4) h^(-2)`, so the second-derivative test is the wrong tool and Kusmin–Landau is the right one.
declarations.name: wideD3_cells_flat

declarations.doc: **Regime B, case (a): the dyadic Kusmin–Landau total is the printed second term.** A cell total `(ℓ/q)^(1/2)` summed over `1.5 h P^(1/2)` cells, with `ℓ ≤ 0.95 P^(1/2)/h` and `q ≥ 0.946 u P^(-1/4)`, gives `≤ 1.6 (h/u)^(1/2) P^(7/8)`. Written at `P = p^8` (so `P^(1/2) = p^4`, `P^(3/8) = p^3`, `P^(7/8) = p^7`) and with the two square roots cleared.
declarations.name: wideD3_caseA_total

declarations.doc: **Regime B, case (b) is confined to small `uh`.** `|D_i| < q/(2ℓ)` forces `φ''` within `O(u h P^(-3/4))` of `½ u h P^(-3/4)`, so `|φ''| ≤ Φ₂` confines the case to `u h ≤ 6 k h₁ h₂ P^(1/8)`.
declarations.name: wideD3_caseB_confined

declarations.doc: **Where case (b) closes outright.** Its second term is `1.1 u P^(3/4)`, inside `P^(7/8)` exactly when `u ≤ 0.9 P^(1/8)`. At `P = p^8`: `1.1 u p^6 ≤ p^7` iff `u ≤ 0.9 p`.
declarations.name: wideD3_caseB_closes

declarations.doc: **Case (b) confines the decoration.** Its defining condition `|Ψ' - q/ℓ| < q/(2ℓ)` with `q/ℓ = (27/16) u h ν^(-3/4)` and `Ψ' = (27/32) u h ν^(-3/4) + φ''` pins `0 < φ'' < (27/16) u h ν^(-3/4)`. So in the only case left open, `|φ''|` is at most `27/16` times `u h ν^(-3/4)` -- the wide budget is never attained there.
declarations.name: wideD3_caseB_confines_phi

declarations.doc: The confinement in the form used: `φ''` is at most `4.83` times the Stage-4 curvature `0.35 u h ν^(-3/4)`, since `(27/16)/0.35 = 4.821…`.
declarations.name: wideD3_caseB_ratio

declarations.doc: **The cell frequencies have bounded gaps.** In case (b), `Ψ' ∈ [27/32, 81/32] u h ν^(-3/4)`, so with `ℓ = (2/3) ν^(1/2)/h` the gaps `α_{i+1} - α_i = Ψ' ℓ` lie in `[0.562, 1.688] u P^(-1/4)`: a strictly increasing sequence of bounded ratio `3`.
declarations.name: wideD3_caseB_gaps

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3.9, the `r = 3` piece.** Where `|f'''|` is good at full scale, `f''` is strictly monotone and any two points of `{|f''| ≤ V}` are within `2V/c`. In the manuscript `c = c₃S/P`, giving the length `2PV/(c₃S)` — the `O(PV/S)` term of Lemma 3.9(i). The mean value theorem is *used* here, not assumed.
declarations.name: sublevel_diam_of_deriv_lower

declarations.doc: **Strong convexity, midpoint form.** If `t ↦ g t - (c/2)t²` is convex then `g` satisfies the midpoint inequality with quadratic defect `(c/8)(y-x)²`. This is exactly what `g'' ≥ c` supplies, and it is the only consequence of the `r = 4` hypothesis that the length bound uses.
declarations.name: midpoint_defect_of_convexOn

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3.9, the `r = 4` piece.** Where `|f''''|` is good at full scale, `f''` is strongly convex (after a sign flip) and the sublevel set has diameter at most `4√(V/c)`. In the manuscript `c = c₄S/P²`, giving `P(V/(c₄S))^(1/2)` — the `(V/S)^(1/2)` term of Lemma 3.9(i), and the term that produces the exponent `89/96`. The hypothesis `hmid` is the `≤ 2 zeros` structure: on the piece, `f''` does not dip below `-V` between the two points.
declarations.name: sublevel_diam_of_strong_convexity

declarations.doc: The two bounds combined, in the shape Lemma 3.9(i) prints: the `r = 3` piece contributes `O(PV/S)` and the `r = 4` piece `O(P(V/S)^(1/2))`, and since `V ≤ S` the second dominates. This is why the manuscript displays only `C(E) P (W/S)^(1/2)`.
declarations.name: sublevel_second_term_dominates

declarations.doc: **Step 5b, the raised-threshold device.** Lemma 3.9 is applied to the global interpolant `Λ` at threshold `W = V + E`, where `E` bounds `|f - Λ|`. Off the sublevel set `{|Λ| ≤ W}` this returns control of `f` itself: `|f| ≥ V`, and `f` carries the sign of `Λ`. This is what makes the former comparison `V ≥ 10 |f - Λ|` unnecessary. The factor `10` was not merely margin: it forced `V` upward exactly where the Lemma 3.9 hypothesis `V ≤ c₇S/2` forced it down, so the two pinned the normalisation `κ` near `1/3`. With this lemma `κ` falls to `1/12`, and both `P₀` and the non-vacuity point `P₁` improve together.
declarations.name: sublevel_raised_threshold

declarations.doc: The device is sound for *any* nonnegative `V`, in particular for the small `V` that the old comparison forbade: the admissible range is `[0, c₇S/2 - E]`, not `[10E, c₇S/2]`.
declarations.name: raised_threshold_admissible

declarations.doc: Row `s3s1-window`. Lemma 3.7's hypothesis `T ≥ 8(1+|B|)` at `T = P^(1/2)` with `|B| < 1/2`. `P = t²`, `t ≥ 12`; `P ≥ 144`.
declarations.name: row_s3s1_window

declarations.doc: Row `s3s1-Bsmall`. `2.25 P^(-1/16) < 1/2`, the inequality naming the regime. `P = t^16`, `t ≥ 4.6`; `P ≥ 4.02·10^10`.
declarations.name: row_s3s1_Bsmall

declarations.doc: Row `s3s2-window`. `P^(1/2) ≥ 8(1 + 2.25 P^(1/4))`, i.e. `t² ≥ 8 + 18t` under `P = t⁴`; first true at `t = 9 + √89 = 18.434`, printed `t ≥ 19`.
declarations.name: row_s3s2_window

declarations.doc: `0.5916 ≤ √0.35`, the rational substitute for the irrational constant in the window-boundary row.
declarations.name: sqrt_0_35_lower

declarations.doc: `0.7483 ≤ √0.56`, the rational substitute in the two Step 5 balance rows. `0.56` is Lemma 5.2b's corrected `λ₀` floor; it is not the `0.35` above.
declarations.name: sqrt_0_56_lower

declarations.doc: Row `stage2-modecurv`. Mode-versus-cell curvature ratio `0.39 P^(1/8) ≥ 4`; `P = t^8`, `t ≥ 10.26`, `P ≥ 1.23·10^8`.
declarations.name: row_stage2_modecurv

declarations.doc: Row `stage5-band`. The collision band needs `4.5 - 1.5/(hP^(1/2)) ≥ 4.4` at `h = 1`; `P = t²`, `t ≥ 15`, `P ≥ 225`.
declarations.name: row_stage5_band

declarations.doc: Row `claimG-pref`. The prefactor `96 P^(-5/24) ≤ 1`; `P = t^24`, `t ≥ 2.5`, `P ≥ 3.6·10^9`.
declarations.name: row_claimG_pref

declarations.doc: Row `claimG-P36`. `P^(1/72 - 1/24) = P^(-1/36) ≤ 1`, i.e. `1 ≤ t` under `P = t^36`. Holds for every `P ≥ 1`; the content is the exponent arithmetic.
declarations.name: row_claimG_P36

declarations.doc: Row `st3b-window`. The same at `0.5 P^(22/48) ≥ 15 P^(9/48)`.
declarations.name: row_st3b_window

declarations.doc: Row `st3a-flat`. Flat cost `16 h₁P^(1/2) + 30 k h₁h₂P^(5/8) ≤ 46 P^(3/4)`, i.e. `16 t^25 + 30 t^36 ≤ 46 t^36` under `P = t^48`. Holds for every `P ≥ 1`.
declarations.name: row_st3a_flat

declarations.doc: Row `st6D1-window`. Stage 6(D1) needs `P^(1/2) ≥ 8(1 + 5P^(1/4))`, i.e. `t² ≥ 8 + 40t`; the paper prints `P^(1/4) ≥ 40.20`, and `t ≥ 41` certifies it. The `5` is the collected widened `θ`-coefficient at Lemma 5.1(iii)'s corrected offset bound `|j| ≤ 2`; at the printed `|j| ≤ 3` it was `7`, and `t ≥ 57`.
declarations.name: row_st6D1_window

declarations.doc: Row `st6D1-modeindex`. Lemma 5.2(iii) closes its mode accounting with `|w| ≤ |B₀| + R₀ ≤ 2R₀`, which needs the widened `θ`-coefficient under Stage 2's truncation: `5P^(1/4) ≤ R₀ = P^(5/16)`. With `P = t^16` that is `5t⁴ ≤ t⁵`, i.e. `t ≥ 5`, so `P ≥ 5^16 = 1.53·10^11`. Alone among the rows this one is *exact* rather than conservative: `t₀ = 5` is the crossing. Appendix A.6 does not tabulate it, and it is what pins `R₀` from below. At the printed offset bound `|j| ≤ 3` the constant is `7` and the row reads `P ≥ 7^16 = 3.32·10^13`, which would make it the largest `c₇`-free row and cut A.5's lever from `120` to `1.08`. See `BranchFreeze.offset_abs_le_two`.
declarations.name: row_st6D1_modeindex

declarations.doc: Row `5b-j0-window`. At `j = 0` the sawtooth has `|B| ≤ 6`, so Lemma 3.7 needs `P^(1/2) ≥ 8(1+6) = 56`; `P = t²`, `P ≥ 3136`.
declarations.name: row_5b_j0_window

declarations.doc: Row `5b-Npieces`. The common refinement of gap cells, anchor runs and sawtooth windows has at most `3.5 P^(13/24)` pieces. Under `P = t^48`: cells `3t^26 + 2`, anchor runs `22t^15`, windows `5t^16`, against `3.5t^26`. `t ≥ 1.46`, `P ≥ 7.7·10^7`.
declarations.name: row_5b_Npieces

declarations.doc: Row `5b-lam0-range`, upper half. Lemma 5.2b's `λ₀ ∈ [0.62, 3.90]` opened to `[0.56, 4.2]`: the `O(P^(-1/4))` and the `±1` in the `β`-bounds must not push `3.90` past `4.2`. Clearing denominators with `P = t⁴` gives `3.90(t+1)(3t²+1)² ≤ 37.8 t^5`; `t ≥ 17`, `P ≥ 8.4·10^4`.
declarations.name: row_5b_lam0_upper

declarations.doc: Row `5b-lam0-range`, lower half: `0.62(t-1)(3t²-1)² ≥ 5.04 t^5`.
declarations.name: row_5b_lam0_lower

declarations.doc: Row `39-beta`. The `β̃`-substitution error `2.31 P^(-1/2) ≤ ρ₀`; `P = t²`, `t ≥ 4288`, `P ≥ 1.8·10^7`.
declarations.name: row_39_beta

declarations.doc: Row `39-wave`. The wave remainder `(3750/7) P^(-5/6) ≤ ρ₀`; `P = t^6`, `t ≥ 15.9`, `P ≥ 1.6·10^7`. The `3750/7 = 300/0.56` carries both the corrected floor and the `u`-cap `300` that rose with it.
declarations.name: row_39_wave

declarations.doc: Row `5a-competitors`. Every Step 5a competitor ratio is `≤ 1/4` (domination at margin 4). Under `P = t^48` the four ratios are `1.3 t^(-6)`, `13 t^(-27)`, `9 t^(-52)`, `3 t^(-6)`; the last binds. `t ≥ 1.52`, `P ≥ 5.4·10^8`.
declarations.name: row_5a_competitors

declarations.doc: Row `5b-E<=c7S`. The interpolant error alone against the Lemma 3.9 budget: `E ≤ c₇S/2` at `S = 0.56 P^(-5/8)`. Multiplying by `P^(5/8)` and substituting `P = t^48` gives `170.6 + 0.11 t^10 ≤ (7/5800) t^20`. This is the floor of the method as `κ → 0`: `t ≥ 1.84`, `P ≥ 4.1·10^12`.
declarations.name: row_5b_E_only

declarations.doc: Row `5a-W<=c7S`. Step 5a's balance comparison at the larger scale `S ≥ 0.60 P^(-5/8)`: `(1/12)√0.6 t^13 + 0.11 t^10 + 170.6 ≤ (3/2320) t^20`, with `(1/12)√0.6 ≤ 0.06455`. The `0.60` is Step E's own floor and did not move with the erratum; only `E` did. `t ≥ 1.91`, `P ≥ 2.9·10^13`.
declarations.name: row_5a_binding

declarations.doc: **Row `5b-W<=c7S`: this is `P₀`.** Step 5b's balance comparison at the lower end `S = 0.56 P^(-5/8)`, with `V = (1/12)S^(1/2)P^(-11/24)`, `E = 170.6 P^(-25/24) + 0.11 P^(-5/6)` and `c₇ = 1/232`. Multiplying by `P^(5/8)` and substituting `P = t^48` gives `a t^13 + 0.11 t^10 + 170.6 ≤ b t^20` with `a = (1/12)√0.56 ≤ 0.06237` and `b = 0.56/464 = 7/5800`. `t ≥ 1.92`, i.e. `P ≥ 4.0·10^13`; the probe's bisection reports `3.59·10^13`. This row is the maximum over all thirty, hence `P₀`. Both `a` and `b` grew with the corrected anchor, `a` as a square root and `b` linearly, which is why the row closes earlier than it did at `0.35`.
declarations.name: row_5b_binding

declarations.doc: Row `thm63-rem`. The Lemma 6.2 linearization remainder `P^(43/96)` is inside `P^(1 - 1/96) = P^(95/96)`; `P = t^96`. Holds for every `P ≥ 1`.
declarations.name: row_thm63_rem

declarations.doc: **Lemma 5.2b, step (i).** The frozen gap satisfies `G = ⌊δ⌋ + κ` with `κ ∈ {0,1}`, so `|G - δ| = |κ - Int.fract δ| ≤ 1`. This is the bound that produces the `84.375 k(h₁+h₂)P^(-9/8)` of the interpolant error.
declarations.name: gap_error_le_one

declarations.doc: The bound `1` is **attained**: at `δ` an integer and `κ = 1`.
declarations.name: gap_error_one_attained

declarations.doc: **Recentring cannot halve it.** The error `κ - Int.fract δ` ranges over a set of diameter `> 1` — it contains `1` (at `κ = 1`, `δ = 0`) and `-3/4` (at `κ = 0`, `δ = 3/4`) — so no constant shift `θ` of the interpolant brings every value within `1/2`. This is why the paper's `1` is not replaced by `1/2`.
declarations.name: gap_error_not_halved_by_recentring

declarations.doc: Exact rotation rule: the letter at position `k` with `a` odd letters already used is even iff `2^(k+1) ≤ 3^a` (that is, `u ≥ 1`).
declarations.name: hugIsEven

declarations.doc: Number of odd letters among the first `k` letters of the exact hug itinerary.
declarations.name: hugOdds

declarations.doc: Letter of the exact hug itinerary at position `k` (`true` = even).
declarations.name: hugLetter

declarations.doc: The exact hug itinerary of length `L`.
declarations.name: hugWord

declarations.doc: Lower window invariant: the exact rule never lets the walk go negative — `2^k ≤ 3^(hugOdds k)`, that is `u_k ≥ 0`.
declarations.name: hugOdds_pow_ge

declarations.doc: Upper window invariant: the exact rule never overshoots — `3^(hugOdds k) < 3·2^k`, the subtraction-free form of `3^(hugOdds k − 1) < 2^k`, that is `u_k < 1 + α`.
declarations.name: hugOdds_pow_lt

declarations.doc: Minimality: `hugOdds k` is the least odd budget with `2^k ≤ 3^a`. This is the integer form of `o_min(k) = ⌈k log 2 / log 3⌉` and the "forcing exactly `o_min` odds" clause of Paper A Lemma 5.6.
declarations.name: hugOdds_least

declarations.doc: Strict lower window for positive prefix lengths: powers of two and three never meet, so `2^k < 3^(hugOdds k)`. Hence `hugOdds k` is exactly the finance table's `o_min(k) = min {o : 3^o > 2^k}`: it satisfies the strict inequality, and `hugOdds_least` gives minimality among all such budgets.
declarations.name: hugOdds_pow_gt

declarations.doc: Combinatorial core of the hug exchange (Paper A Theorem 5.4): the exact hug itinerary is prefix-minimal among admissible exponent walks. Admissibility of an odd-count profile `a` at prefix `k` is `u_k ≥ 0`, in integer form `2^k ≤ 3^(a k)`.
declarations.name: hugOdds_le_of_admissible

declarations.doc: **Cycle itineraries dominate the hug itinerary** (corollary of `cycleMin_prefix_pow_le` and `hugOdds_least`): on a minimum-based cycle itinerary, every prefix carries at least as many odd letters as the exact hug itinerary of the same length. This is the cycle-native form of the hug adversary — the rotation itinerary is the pointwise cheapest odd-count profile any hypothetical cycle can present.
declarations.name: cycleMin_prefix_odds_ge_hug

declarations.doc: Full-itinerary instance: a minimum-based cycle itinerary of length `L` has at least `hugOdds L` odd letters.
declarations.name: cycleMin_odds_ge_hug

declarations.doc: One step adds at most one odd letter.
declarations.name: hugOdds_succ_le

declarations.doc: The odd count is monotone in the prefix length.
declarations.name: hugOdds_mono

declarations.doc: The odd count grows at most linearly: `hugOdds (j + m) ≤ hugOdds j + m`.
declarations.name: hugOdds_add_le

declarations.doc: Budgeted hug rule at total length `L`, odd budget `o`, position `k`, with `a` odd letters already used: forced even when the odd budget is exhausted, forced odd when the remaining letters must all be odd, otherwise the exact rule.
declarations.name: budgetedIsEven

declarations.doc: Number of odd letters among the first `k` letters of the budgeted hug itinerary at `(L, o)`.
declarations.name: budgetedOdds

declarations.doc: The budgeted hug itinerary at `(L, o)`.
declarations.name: budgetedWord

declarations.doc: At the exact budget `o = hugOdds L`, neither budget clause fires: the budgeted rule at position `k < L` with the exact count agrees with the exact letter.
declarations.name: budgetedIsEven_hug

declarations.doc: At the exact budget, the budgeted and exact odd counts agree at every prefix.
declarations.name: budgetedOdds_eq_hugOdds

declarations.doc: **Itinerary identity** (Paper A Lemma 5.6, discrete side): the budgeted hug itinerary at `(L, hugOdds L)` equals the exact hug `L`-prefix. Together with `hugOdds_pow_ge` and `hugOdds_least` this says the exact rule forces exactly the minimal admissible odd budget, so the budget never binds.
declarations.name: budgetedWord_eq_hugWord

declarations.doc: Sanity instance: the record length `L = 84` has exact odd budget `53`, matching the finance table.
declarations.name: hugOdds_84

declarations.doc: Sanity instance: the generator `L = 1054` has exact odd budget `665`, matching `three_pow_step_gt_two_pow_step`.
declarations.name: hugOdds_1054

declarations.doc: Sanity instance: the window seed `L = 50508` has exact odd budget `31867`, matching the finance table.
declarations.name: hugOdds_seed

declarations.doc: Lattice bridge: the survivor-lattice base point `(Lstar, Ostar) = (25781, 16266)` of `RunSurvivorLattice.lean` is a hug pair — its odd count is the exact hug count at its length. Together with `hugOdds_1054` (the step generator `(1054, 665)`) and `hugOdds_seed` (the seed `(50508, 31867) = 2·(25781, 16266) − (1054, 665)`), all survivor-lattice generators lie on the hug diagonal `o = hugOdds L`.
declarations.name: hugOdds_lattice_base

declarations.doc: The hug counts along the certified convergent denominators of `θ` (`theta_convergent_denominators` in `OstrowskiSandwich.lean`): these are the finance table's `o_min` values at each block length.
declarations.name: hugOdds_convergent_denoms

declarations.doc: The charge is antitone in the weight: heavier states are cheaper to visit. This is the paper's "`g` is strictly decreasing in `u`" in the (non-strict) form the envelope uses.
declarations.name: stateCharge_antitone

declarations.doc: The hug weight is pointwise below every admissible weight profile (real form of `hugOdds_le_of_admissible`).
declarations.name: hugWeight_le_of_admissible

declarations.doc: On a minimum-based cycle, the hug weight is pointwise below the realized walk weight (real form of `cycleMin_prefix_odds_ge_hug`).
declarations.name: hugWeight_le_walkWeight

declarations.doc: **Hug charge maximality.** For any admissible odd-count profile `a` (every prefix satisfies `2^k ≤ 3^{a k}`) and any reduced log-base `ν > 0`, the total walk charge is at most the hug charge. This is the analytic half of Paper A Theorem 5.4, strengthened from the fixed-`(L,o)` class to all admissible walks.
declarations.name: hug_charge_maximal

declarations.doc: **Defect sum is bounded by the walk charge at the reduced base.** On a minimum-based cycle with `n ≥ 400` and positive reduced log-base `ν = log n − D`, each cyclic defect `1/(x_k log x_k)` is bounded by the charge of the realized weight: exponentiating the transport inequality gives `x_k ≥ e^{w_k ν}` and `log x_k ≥ w_k ν`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_defect_le_charge

declarations.doc: **Defect sum is bounded by the hug charge at the reduced base** (the §5.2 consequence composed with Theorem 5.4): on a minimum-based cycle with `n ≥ 400` and positive reduced log-base, the cyclic defect sum is at most the hug charge of the same length. This is the full structural half of the walk-charge envelope; only the rotation average and Denjoy–Koksma evaluation of the right-hand side remain analytic.
declarations.name: cycleMin_defect_le_hug_charge

declarations.doc: Parameterized majorant `−log(1−t) ≤ c·t` for `0 ≤ t ≤ 1 − 1/c`: `log(1/(1−t)) ≤ t/(1−t)` and `1/(1−t) ≤ c` on the threshold interval. Instances: `c = 1.05` on `t ≤ 1/21` (transport) and `c = 6/5` on `t ≤ 1/6` (defect finance).
declarations.name: neg_log_one_sub_le_mul

declarations.doc: Even step, lower side: for even `x ≥ 441`, `log T(x) ≥ (1/2)·log x − 1.05/√x`.
declarations.name: log_floorPower_even_ge

declarations.doc: Odd step, lower side: for odd `x ≥ 9`, `log T(x) ≥ (3/2)·log x − 1.05/(x·√x)`.
declarations.name: log_floorPower_odd_ge

declarations.doc: One more letter adds one to the odd count exactly when that letter is odd.
declarations.name: oddCount_take_succ

declarations.doc: An odd letter multiplies the walk weight by `3/2`.
declarations.name: walkWeight_succ_odd

declarations.doc: An even letter halves the walk weight.
declarations.name: walkWeight_succ_even

declarations.doc: Above-anchor prefixes keep `w_k ≥ 1` (`aboveAnchor_prefix_pow_le` in weight form).
declarations.name: one_le_walkWeight_aboveAnchor

declarations.doc: Cycle minimality forces `u_k ≥ 0`, that is `w_k ≥ 1` (`cycleMin_prefix_pow_le` in weight form).
declarations.name: one_le_walkWeight

declarations.doc: The walk weight is never negative.
declarations.name: walkWeight_nonneg

declarations.doc: One-step recurrence for the running prefix deficit.
declarations.name: prefixDeficit_succ

declarations.doc: The prefix deficit is monotone in the prefix length.
declarations.name: prefixDeficit_mono

declarations.doc: The prefix deficit in closed count form.
declarations.name: prefixDeficit_eq

declarations.doc: The full-itinerary prefix deficit is the transport deficit.
declarations.name: prefixDeficit_length

declarations.doc: Upper envelope on any realized prefix (floors only lose): `log x_k ≤ w_k · log n`. Log form of `power_bound_word`; no anchor hypothesis.
declarations.name: follows_log_le_walkWeight

declarations.doc: Transport invariant along a descent-free prefix: `w_k·(log n − D_k) ≤ log x_k` with the running prefix deficit. The single transport induction; the cycle form is the closed instance.
declarations.name: aboveAnchor_transport_prefix

declarations.doc: **Transport on descent-free prefixes** (log form): on `AboveAnchor n w` with `n ≥ 400`, every state satisfies `w_k·(log n − D) ≤ log x_k` with `D = 1.05·e/n + 0.7·o/(n·√n)`.
declarations.name: aboveAnchor_transport

declarations.doc: Transport invariant along the cycle: closed instance of `aboveAnchor_transport_prefix`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_transport_prefix

declarations.doc: **Transport to a reduced base** (Paper A Theorem 5.3, log form): on a minimum-based cycle with minimum `n ≥ 400`, every state satisfies `w_k·(log n − D) ≤ log x_k` with `D = 1.05·e/n + 0.7·o/(n·√n)`. Exponentiating gives `x_k ≥ (n e^{−D})^{w_k}`. Closed instance of `aboveAnchor_transport`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_transport

declarations.doc: **Flight envelope** (fly-height sandwich): on a descent-free prefix with anchor `n ≥ 400`, `w_k·(log n − D) ≤ log x_k ≤ w_k·log n`. At the prefix peak `H` with `W = max_k w_k` this gives `W·(log n − D) ≤ log H ≤ W·log n`: the fly exponent `log H / log n` equals the peak walk weight up to `O(D·W/log n)`. Not a halt theorem and not a divergence theorem.
declarations.name: aboveAnchor_flight_envelope

declarations.doc: Weight form of a walk-height hypothesis: `2^(k+B) ≤ 3^{a_k}` (the exponent walk is at height `≥ B` doublings at step `k`) gives `2^B ≤ w_k` for the walk weight `w_k = 3^{a_k}/2^k`.
declarations.name: two_pow_le_walkWeight

declarations.doc: **Walk-height law** (divergence rate): on a descent-free prefix with anchor `n ≥ 400`, a walk height of `B` doublings at step `k` (`2^(k+B) ≤ 3^{a_k}`) forces `2^B·(log n − D) ≤ log x_k`; exponentiating, `x_k ≥ (n·e^{−D})^{2^B}` — heights along a descent-free prefix are doubly exponential in the walk height. Composed with the walk-divergence theorem (`J-flight-walk-divergence`; human glue: pigeonhole plus `cycle_strict_envelope`), every descent-free flight realizes this rate along an unbounded walk. Not a halt theorem and not a divergence theorem.
declarations.name: aboveAnchor_height_of_walk

declarations.doc: `q_{n-k}` with value `0` when `k > n`.
declarations.name: qShift

declarations.doc: `E_i(s) = s₁ q_{i-2} + s₂ q_{i-1} + s₃ q_i`.
declarations.name: energy

declarations.doc: Coefficient row `u_i = (q_{i-2}, q_{i-1}, q_i)`.
declarations.name: adjointU

declarations.doc: Left action of `A = [[0, 0, 3], [1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 2]]` on a row vector.
declarations.name: mulRowA

declarations.doc: Constructional identity: `E_{i-1}(T_w s) = E_i(s) - w q_{i-1}`.

declarations.doc: `∑_t ws[t] * q (start - 1 - t)`. Matches Python `consumed_sum`.
declarations.name: consumedSum

declarations.doc: After an MSD word of length `k` from remaining `n+k`, `E_n(fold s) = E_{n+k}(s) - ∑_j w_j q_{n+k-1-j}`. KNOWN packaging of `energy_step`, not a bound on `L₀`.
declarations.name: energy_telescope

declarations.doc: MSD recurrence word `B* = (1,-2,-1,-3)`. `val(B*) = q_{n+3}-2q_{n+2}-q_{n+1}-3q_n = 0`. KNOWN `q_rec`, not `L₀`.

declarations.doc: The set of integer controls `w` with `E_{n-1}(T_w s)` in a fixed interval `[lo, hi]` is consecutive. This is `energy_step` plus `q > 0`, not a bound on `L₀`.
declarations.name: energy_control_interval

declarations.doc: `∑ q`-weights of a zero word vanish.
declarations.name: consumedSum_replicate_zero

declarations.doc: Homogeneous motion `A^k = T_0^k` preserves energy in the sliding index: `E_n(A^k s) = E_{n+k}(s)`. This is `energy_telescope` on the zero word, not a bound on `L₀`.
declarations.name: energy_homogeneous

declarations.doc: Determinant of three row vectors.
declarations.name: tripleDet

declarations.doc: Consecutive adjoints are independent: `det = 3^{n-2}` for `n ≥ 2`. Neighboring energies invert `s` over `ℚ`. Not a bound on `L₀`.
declarations.name: adjointDet_eq

declarations.doc: Homogeneous residual matrix `A`. `step 0 = A`.
declarations.name: applyA

declarations.doc: Affine unfolding: `T_ws(s) = A^{|ws|} s + T_ws(0)`.
declarations.name: foldSteps_affine

declarations.doc: Control particular from the origin: `s = −∑_j A^{k-1-j} e₃ w_j`. KNOWN variation of constants, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: particularSum

declarations.doc: From the origin, an MSD word unfolds by variation of constants: `foldSteps ws origin = particularSum ws`.
declarations.name: origin_particular

declarations.doc: From the origin, `(c_B)₃ = -val(B)`. KNOWN energy at `n=0`, not `L₀`.

declarations.doc: From any start state, `(T_B(s))₃ = E_{|B|}(s) - val(B)`. KNOWN `energy_telescope` at remaining 0, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: fold_s3

declarations.doc: Length-`n` suffix acceptance is classified by the energy, not by residual coordinates: `foldSteps ws s` lands on `F` exactly when `energy |ws| s` equals the consumed sum of `ws`.
declarations.name: fold_on_F_iff

declarations.doc: Length-`|ws|` landing on `F` is classified by `E_{|ws|}`, not by `s`. KNOWN `fold_on_F_iff`, not a Myhill–Nerode calculus and not `L₀`.
declarations.name: same_energy_same_OnF

declarations.doc: Concatenation of particulars: `c_{UV} = A^{|V|} c_U + c_V`.

declarations.doc: Origin reset prefixes do not change the particular of a suffix. KNOWN `particular_concat` at `c_R=0`, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: reset_prefix

declarations.doc: Two-start MSD split. Not `val(U) + C val(V)`. KNOWN, not `L₀`.

declarations.doc: `val(UV) = val(V) - E_{|V|}(c_U)`. KNOWN packaging, not `L₀`.

declarations.name: q

For every finite U, the origin-reachable residual equals λℤ intersect the symmetric invariant interval.

If λ is not divisible by 3 and s≠t, the constant word of any letter of length v_3(s-t)+1 distinguishes the output streams of F_{λ,U}(s,u)=λ·D(s+u) with output lsd(s+u). Distinct residuals are therefore Mealy-inequivalent, so M(λ,U)=|R_{λ,U}| on every nonempty origin-reachable machine in this regime.
At λ=3, translation by 3k preserves every output stream: signedTrace 3 (s+3k) w = signedTrace 3 s w. This symmetry is not origin-reachable when max|u|≤1.
Identical immediate lsd signatures force behavioral equivalence of residual states.
If 3^L divides s-t and |w|≤L, then the lsd streams of F_{λ,U} from s and t agree on w. A remaining-horizon L controller therefore merges (s,q_L) and (t,q_L) whenever that congruence holds.
If λ is not divisible by 3, s≠t, and |w|≥v_3(s-t)+1, then the lsd streams differ on w. Finite horizon preserves residual distinguishability exactly when a legal word of that length exists.

If λ is not divisible by 3 and s≠t, the lsd streams of F_{λ,U} agree on a word w if and only if |w|≤v_3(s-t). A finite control language therefore merges (s,q) and (t,q) exactly when every legal word is shorter than v_3(s-t)+1.
Accelerated T is well-defined on positive odd integers.
Direct residue formula for R
Affine-center numerator identities
Expanding periods excluded; D divides C; even amplitude
Kramer endpoint / 2-adic endpoint congruences
Affine gap recurrence
n* ≤ n for finite valuation codes
Positive integer realizer iff eventual zero lift.
The shortcut map C(n)=n/2 (even) or (3n+1)/2 (odd) is well-defined on positive integers, and {1,2} is a 2-cycle.
V(n)=n strictly decreases on every shortcut step.
For every L≥1, n=2^L-1 realises L odd shortcut steps and C^L(n)=3^L-1>n. No residual n mod 2^L with blocks of length at most L certifies strict descent.

AboveAnchor walk nonnegativity and hug domination: the Section 5 discrete walk layer ported from cycles to open trajectories. If AboveAnchor(n,w) with n >= 2, then every prefix length k <= |w| satisfies 2^k <= 3^{oddCount(w.take k)} (aboveAnchor_prefix_pow_le, AboveAnchorWalk.lean): a never-descending orbit segment keeps the exponent walk u_k >= 0, exactly the CycleMin hypothesis of cycleMin_prefix_pow_le with no cycle, by composing the defect-free upper envelope power_bound_contracts with the anchor hypothesis. Composed with hug minimality (hugOdds_least), every above-anchor prefix dominates the exact hug itinerary in odd count: hugOdds k <= oddCount(w.take k) (aboveAnchor_prefix_odds_ge_hug; full-word form aboveAnchor_odds_ge_hug). Hence a hypothetical descent-free flight carries odd density at least log 2 / log 3 in every prefix, and the hug adversary prices open descent-free flight, not only hypothetical cycles. This constrains hypothetical non-terminating orbit segments only: not a halt theorem, not a descent-certificate existence claim, and not a cycle obstruction.

Hypothesis: recurrent hug domination (flight note Sec. 5.5) forces O(y) >= O*(y) at every scale for every persistent divergent orbit, so that every Clotho basin is every-block unconditionally. Refuted twice. Structurally: every flight-note law bounds escape from below - a_k >= hugOdds(k) (aboveAnchor_prefix_odds_ge_hug), u_k >= 0, u_k >= log2(log x_k / log n), hug excess to infinity, linear peak growth - and none bounds it from above; the gate O(y) >= O*(y) is an upper bound on escape speed and nothing in the laboratory supplies one. Empirically: on the seven canonical high-flyers, at the first passage of every recorded decade from 1e6 to 1e5000, the gate is never met; the walk gain per odd step at passage is 0.08..0.58 against gates of 0.0006..0.04, between 28 and 650 times too fast (slowest passage: 1122603 at 1e5000, O = 67 odd steps in 96, gain 0.145, 240 times the gate 0.0006; 48443 reaches 1e5000 in 31 steps with 26 odd). Random odd starts near 1e6 never meet it either. So the Clotho every-block statement (J-clotho-basin-every-block-criterion) stays conditional on slow escape, and slow escape is neither forced nor observed: a persistent thread whose basin is every-block would be unlike every flight ever realised. Excludes nothing; not a halt theorem.

If a Juggler cycle itinerary based at n ends with r ≥ 1 even letters, the state immediately before that trailing even run is strictly less than (n+1)^{2^r}. The case r = 1 is the last-even one-step preimage; r = 2 is the two-even bound of Paper A Lemma 3.5 on OOOOEE; r = 3 is the three-even bound for OOOOOOEEE. Lean theorem cycle_trailing_evens_lt. This is a one-step-preimage identity, not a leftover exclusion and not a halt theorem.

On a Juggler CycleMin start n ≥ 2 with word w of length L and oddCount o, the dyadic-cell logarithm bound log z ≤ 2 log y + 2/y unrolls to n · log n · (3^o − 2^L) ≤ L · 3^o (Paper A Theorem 4.4; Lean cycleMin_finance). Every cycle state is at least 12 and the rotated minimum is odd, so the minimum is at least 13 and 13 log 13 > 65/2, hence (65/2)(3^o − 2^L) ≤ L · 3^o for every CycleItinerary (cycle_finance_min_thirteen). This is the whole-cycle financing of the formal expansion 2^L < 3^o by relative floor defects. It is not a halt theorem, not an exclusion of every length, and not the computational 6/5 table used for L ≤ 10^5.

Per-block law of the E-closure of a finite seed set S: on the dyadic block B the density equals sum over x in S and k >= 1 of |[x^(2^k), (x+1)^(2^k)) meet B| times 2^(-k) / |B|; verified to 0.5 percent (measured/predicted 0.996..1.005) on a 40-seed closure to 4e7. One landing burst from x contributes S/(x B) in (1/x, 2/x], S = x^(2^k); OE bursts land at clock offset log2(4/3), in other blocks (six blocks of the test carry OE density with zero E density), adding 8..32 percent where both land. Hence for a Lachesis basin, whose cycle states land in every block by J-lachesis-basin-every-block, the E-visible density on a block at scale y is at least (1/ln y) sum_{x in C} 1/x and the E+OE part at most (3/ln y) sum_{x in C} 1/x. Finance's Lean inv-sum form (cycleMin_finance_inv_sum: (3^o - 2^L) ln n <= 3^o sum 1/x) gives sum 1/x >= theta(L) ln n, and every state >= n gives sum 1/x <= L/n; floor > cap is the finance kill of the pair (true at n = 1e10, L = 780239). At n = 3.5e8, L = 780239: sum 1/x in [6.83e-5, 2.23e-3], so on the valid range y >= n^(2^(1 + u_max)) the block density is in [2.97e-7, 2.90e-5] at y = 1e100 and [9.89e-8, 9.68e-6] at y = 1e300, against the single-seed 2/n = 5.7e-9 (the first draft quoted 1e12 and 1e68, below the threshold for u_max >= 2; withdrawn). A cycle that barely survives finance has sum 1/x pinned, hence a basin whose contagion-visible density is pinned to within the constant factor. Not a halt theorem; the full basin's density is bounded above only by the free term.

No itinerary of length at most ten is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2; equivalently a nontrivial Juggler cycle, if one exists, has period at least eleven. Lengths ≤ 8 are the census J-small-cycle-census-eight; lengths 9 and 10 are excluded by the finance inequality at the residual floor 12 (no_cycle_itinerary_length_nine, no_cycle_itinerary_length_ten, packaged as no_cycle_itinerary_length_le_ten). Strengthened by J-small-cycle-census-eleven. This is a Lean companion to Paper A Theorem 4.6, not a leftover-itinerary length-11 census, not a no-cycle-of-any-length theorem, and not a halt theorem.

If a nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary exists at n ≥ 2, its period is 11 or at least 14. Lengths ≤ 10 are J-small-cycle-census-ten; lengths 12 and 13 are excluded by the same finance comparison (no_cycle_itinerary_length_twelve, no_cycle_itinerary_length_thirteen); length 16 is likewise excluded (no_cycle_itinerary_length_sixteen) but is absorbed into the ≥ 14 residual. Lean theorem cycle_itinerary_length_eleven_or_ge_fourteen. Strengthened by J-cycle-itinerary-length-ge-fourteen, which kills the length-11 disjunct. This is not a leftover-itinerary length-11 census, not a no-cycle-of-any-length theorem, and not a halt theorem.

No itinerary of length at most eleven is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2; equivalently a nontrivial Juggler cycle, if one exists, has period at least twelve, and in fact at least fourteen by J-cycle-itinerary-length-ge-fourteen. Strengthened by J-small-cycle-census-eighteen. Length 11 is the first near-convergent (2^11 < 3^7); the residual floor 53 plus cycle_finance_min_fifty_three excludes it (finance_excludes_length_eleven, packaged as no_cycle_itinerary_length_le_eleven). This is a Lean companion to Paper A Theorem 4.6, not a leftover-itinerary census of the thirty length-11 short-gap families, not a theorem named no_cycle_itinerary_length_eleven, not a no-cycle-of-any-length theorem, and not a halt theorem.

If a nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary exists at n ≥ 2, its period is at least 14. Strengthened through J-cycle-itinerary-length-eighty-four-or-ge-eighty-five: lengths 14–83 except the named leftovers along the way are excluded, so the laboratory leftover is period 84 or at least 85. Lean theorem cycle_itinerary_length_ge_fourteen. This is not a no-cycle-of-any-length theorem, and not a halt theorem.

No itinerary of length at most 18 is a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2, except that length 19 is not excluded here. Lengths ≤ 11 are J-small-cycle-census-eleven; lengths 12, 13, and 16 remain excluded at the residual floor 12; lengths 14, 15, 17, and 18 are excluded by cycle_finance_min_fifty_three (finance_excludes_length_fourteen and companions, packaged as no_cycle_itinerary_length_le_eighteen). Strengthened by J-small-cycle-census-nineteen. This is a Lean companion to Paper A Theorem 4.6, not a leftover-itinerary census, not an exclusion of length 19, not a no-cycle-of-any-length theorem, and not a halt theorem.

If a nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary exists at n ≥ 2, its period is 19 or at least 30. Lengths ≤ 18 are J-small-cycle-census-eighteen; lengths 20–29 are excluded by the same floor-53 finance comparison. Length 19 is the next near-convergent (2^19 < 3^12) and survives 371/2; length 30 also survives 371/2. Lean theorems cycle_itinerary_length_nineteen_or_ge_thirty and the weaker corollary cycle_itinerary_length_nineteen_or_ge_twenty. This row is the floor-53 leftover. If a nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary exists at n ≥ 2, and every length in [30, 10^5) outside a named list of near-convergents is already excluded, then the period is 84, or belongs to that list, or is at least 10^5. Lean theorem cycle_itinerary_eliahou_leftover: bookkeeping on cycle_itinerary_length_eighty_four_or_ge_eighty_five plus EliahouTable, not a new inequality. If a nontrivial Juggler cycle exists, there is no period ≤ 25780, and no period ≤ 10^5 outside the 141 near-convergent lengths of ln 2 / ln 3 at the Python floor 10^6 using the length-only parity 6/5 table (Paper A Theorem 4.6). Lengths ≤ 18 are J-small-cycle-census-eighteen; length 19 is the near-convergent 2^19 < 3^12 killed by the residual floor 257 plus cycle_finance_min_two_hundred_fifty_seven (finance_excludes_length_nineteen, packaged as no_cycle_itinerary_length_le_nineteen).
