If a nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary exists at n ≥ 2, its period is at least 30. The floor-53 leftover J-cycle-itinerary-length-nineteen-or-ge-thirty plus finance_excludes_length_nineteen kills the length-19 disjunct. This is not a no-cycle-of-any-length theorem, and not a halt theorem.

If a nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary exists at n ≥ 2, its period is 38 or at least 39. Lengths ≤ 19 are J-small-cycle-census-nineteen; lengths 20–29 remain excluded at the residual floor 53; lengths 30–37 are excluded by cycle_finance_min_two_hundred_fifty_seven. This row is the leftover before the 61/11 log certificate. Strengthened by J-cycle-itinerary-length-fifty-seven-or-ge-fifty-eight, which kills the length-38 disjunct. log 257 > 61/11, via e < 2.7182818286 and e^61 < 257^11 (log_two_hundred_fifty_seven_gt). Combined with the residual floor 257 this gives n log n > 15677/11 on a CycleMin, which excludes cycle length 38. The weaker half-integer bound 11/2 was enough for length 19 but not for 38. If a nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary exists at n ≥ 2, its period is 57 or at least 58. Lengths ≤ 19 are J-small-cycle-census-nineteen; lengths 20–56 are excluded at floor 257. This row is the leftover before the two extra odd seeds 257 and 259. Strengthened by J-cycle-itinerary-length-eighty-four-or-ge-eighty-five, which kills the length-57 disjunct at the residual floor 261. If a nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary exists at n ≥ 2, its period is 84 or at least 85. Lengths ≤ 56 are excluded at floor 257; lengths 57–83 are excluded by cycle_finance_min_two_hundred_sixty_one at 15921/11 (finance_excludes_length_fiftyseven, finance_excludes_length_seventysix, and companions, packaged as no_cycle_itinerary_length_lt_eighty_four). Length 84 is the next record near-convergent (need ≈ 40269). Lean theorem cycle_itinerary_length_eighty_four_or_ge_eighty_five. Strengthened by J-cycle-itinerary-length-eighty-four-m-ge-three-or-ge-eighty-five, which kills length 84 with at most two odd-runs, and by J-cycle-itinerary-eliahou-leftover, which rewrites the length leftover plus the finance table as period 84, a listed near-convergent, or at least 10^5. This is not a no-cycle-of-any-length theorem, and not a halt theorem.

If a nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary exists at n ≥ 2, its period is 84 with at least three odd-runs on a CycleMin rotation, or at least 85. At residual floor 261 the inv-sum form of cycleMin_finance (constant 1) plus a uniform odd-run height cap excludes every length-84 CycleMin with cycleCircuitCount ≤ 2: valleys ≤ m/n, first odds ≤ m/4217, later odds ≤ o/273845, evens ≤ e/n², using floorPower 261 = 4216 and floorPower 4217 = 273845. Lean theorems no_cycleMin_length_eighty_four_of_circuit_le_two and cycle_itinerary_length_eighty_four_m_ge_three_or_ge_eighty_five in CycleHeightFinance.lean. This is not the 6/5 greedy packing of J-cycle-position-finance, not an exclusion of length 84 at m ≥ 3, not a no-cycle-of-any-length theorem, and not a halt theorem.

The thirty first-expanding four-even short-gap leftovers O^{a0} E O^{a1} E O^{a2} E O^{a3} E are not CycleMin words. On a CycleMin every later state is >= n, so the exact cells compose by absorb_odd_step and absorb_even_step: n^A < (n+1)^B (x+1)^γ implies n^{A+γ} < (n+1)^{B+γ} (isqrt(x)+1)^{2γ}. After the prefix, cycle_trailing_evens_lt puts the image below (n+1)^{2^r}. Any 7-odd word that starts O keeps γ a power of two and raises on each later odd, so the slack is identically 3^7-2^{11}=139, independent of even placement. For n >= 30 and A <= 13905 the comparison is (n+1)^{A-139} < n^A; no n with 2 <= n < 30 follows any of the thirty prefixes. The eight leftovers whose only CycleMin-shaped rotation is themselves (OOOOOOOEEEE, OOOOOOEOEEE, OOOOOOEEEOE, OOOOOEOEEOE, OOOOOOEEOEE, OOOOOEOEOEE, OOOOOEEOEOE, OOOOEOEOEOE) are not cycle itineraries. Lean: absorb_even_step, family_slack139, no_cycleMin_cyclemin_fudge, and the named unique-rotation CycleItinerary theorems in CycleMinFudge.lean. This replaces leftover 2-fudge cutoffs 10^8 through 10^15. Not a length-11 census, not no_cycle_itinerary_four_even, not the a0>=8 tails, and not a halt theorem. Not imported by JugglerPaper.

On every start-O four-even Juggler word with o >= 7 odds, the CycleMin exponent machine has slack identically 3^o - 2^{o+4}. After a start-O prefix, A = B + gamma * 2^r + familySlack o, and familySlack o + 2^{o+4} = 3^o because 2^{o+4} <= 3^o. The length-11 case is familySlack 7 = 139. Lean: familySlack, two_pow_add_four_le_three_pow, exponents_slack_add, slack_of_four_even, slack_of_four_even_word in CycleMinFudge.lean. Not a CycleMin exclusion of the tails, not no_cycleMin_four_even, and not a halt theorem. Not imported by JugglerPaper.

An odd state z ≥ (n+1)^2 has odd-step image at least (n+1)^3. Consequently, on OOO at q ≥ 5 the residual is T^3(q) ≥ (q+1)^3, not merely the next-square bound of ooo_suffix_threshold. On a CycleMin whose first odd run has length at least three, the first three-odd residual is at least (n+1)^3. Lean: odd_ge_succ_sq_floorPower_ge_cube, ooo_residual_ge_cube in Preimages.lean; cycleMin_ooo_residual_ge_cube in CycleMinObstruction.lean. The smallest universal local-overshoot A on CycleMin is 2, not 3. Not a halt theorem and not a contained-run prohibition.

On a CycleMin, after the first O^a E with a ≥ 2, an immediate odd run of length at least two overshoots the landing y = T_{O^a E}(n) > n: the next two-odd residual is at least (y+1)^2, hence at least (n+2)^2. Lean: cycleMin_transport_second_oo, cycleMin_transport_second_oo_ge in CycleMinObstruction.lean. The second residual lies outside the last-even one-step preimage when it is not the last even letter. Not a halt theorem, not a four-even assembler, and not a claim that two short odd runs close a cycle.

Every nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary based at n ≥ 2 is formally expanding. Cycle extrema satisfy the certified parity, order, square-scale, and nested-cell constraints; a minimum-based cycle orientation cannot end in an odd letter. The path from a cycle minimum to any later even state is superquadratic. These are necessary cycle restrictions, not an exclusion of all cycles.

The defect-sum finance inequality (the certified identity of Paper A Theorem 4.6, previously human) and the walk-charge kill criterion (Theorem 5.9 mechanism), Lean end to end (DefectFinance.lean). Finance: on a CycleMin cycle with minimum n ≥ 400, 1 − 2^L/3^o ≤ (6/5)·Σ_k 1/(x_k·log x_k) (cycleMin_defect_finance). Ingredients all Lean: per-step floor losses in image form — for a state x with image y = T(x), the relative defect δ = (x^e − y²)/x^e satisfies δ ≤ 2/y and −log(1−δ) ≤ (6/5)δ on δ ≤ 1/6 (neg_log_one_sub_le_sixth), so each step loses at most (6/5)/y in log terms (log_floorPower_even_ge_sub at x ≥ 441, log_floorPower_odd_ge_sub at x ≥ 9), plus the floor-only-loses upper bounds (log_floorPower_even_le, log_floorPower_odd_le); the unroll is the WalkTransport weight induction run twice — upper invariant log x_k ≤ w_k·log n (cycleMin_log_le_weight) pricing the amplification, charged lower invariant w_k(log n − C_k) ≤ log x_k (cycleMin_charge_prefix) accumulating C_k = Σ 1.2·log n/(x_{i+1}·log x_{i+1}) — closed at x_L = n and reindexed cyclically. Kill criterion: chaining with cycleMin_defect_le_hug_charge (WalkChargeMax.lean), every CycleMin at n ≥ 400 with positive reduced log-base ν = log n − D must satisfy 1 − 2^L/3^o ≤ (6/5)·Σ_k g(hugWeight k) at the reduced base (cycleMin_hug_kill_criterion) — the entire finance-vs-hug-charge implication is a single Lean theorem; the per-length numeric kill evaluations (Thm 5.9 tables) remain verified computation, as does the parity refinement of Cor 4.5. Not a cycle obstruction by itself and not a halt theorem.

For a realized Juggler word w, the first positive local remainder sits after a tight even or odd power-of-two prefix. That remainder contributes at least ρ_j^{2^j} to Δ, and the suffix operator Amplify (later remainders dropped) is a lower bound. An odd letter lifts an inserted defect by the exact cubic (x^a+D)^3-x^{3a} ≥ 3 x^{2a} D. Mixed OOE has firstDefect ≤ 1, with Δ ≥ 3 T(n)^4 ρ_0 or Δ ≥ ρ_1^2. These bounds do not claim Δ exceeds the formal surplus.
For every finite Juggler word w realized at n, J^{|w|}(n)^{2^{|w|}} ≤ n^{3^{#O(w)}}. If n ≥ 2 and 3^{#O(w)} < 2^{|w|}, then J^{|w|}(n) < n.

If n ≥ 2, A > 0, x^A ≤ n^B, and B < k·A, then x < n^k. EnvelopeState n x packages the free inequality x^A ≤ n^B, with even (A,B)→(2A,B) and odd (A,B)→(2A,3B). PowerBound is the special case A=2^|w|, B=3^{oddCount w}. A realized itinerary with 3^{oddCount w} < k·2^{|w|} therefore has T_w(n) < n^k. power_bound_contracts is the k=1 case. Escape square and cube cells are k=2 and k=3 instances. The leftover itinerary OOEOOEOOEOEOO has the cube gap 3^9 < 3·2^13 and not the square gap 3^9 < 2·2^13. This is not a halt theorem and not a cycle-exclusion theorem.

Every n satisfies EventuallyCycles n or EscapesToInfinity n. A uniformly bounded trajectory repeats: if T^k(n) ≤ M for every k, then some i < j have T^i(n) = T^j(n). ReachesOne n implies EventuallyCycles n because T(1) = 1. On MinimalNonTerm n a cycle value stays ≥ n. This is not a proof that escape is impossible, not a cycle-exclusion theorem, and not a halt theorem.

If n ≥ 2 follows OOEOOE, then T_OOEOOE(n) < n^2 because x^{64} ≤ n^{81} forbids n^2 ≤ x. If n follows OOEOOEO, then the next image is < n^2 because z^{128} ≤ n^{243} forbids n^2 ≤ z. On MinimalNonTerm n the OOEOOE landing is odd, and the forced next O is followed by another O: an even landing or an even next image below n^2 is descent. The argument does not use a CycleMin return image = n. This is not a proof that escape is impossible, not a Z5 family, not a length-11 census, and not a halt theorem.

If MinimalNonTerm n and n follows w, then w is not an exponent-gap itinerary, and every prefix of w is noncontracting. Contrapositive of power_bound_contracts plus minimal_nonterm_no_descent. Concatenating expanding residual blocks therefore cannot create an exponent certificate on a CE. This is not a proof that escape is impossible and not a halt theorem.

If n ≥ 2 follows OOEOOEOO, then T_OOEOOEOO(n) < n^3 because x^{256} ≤ n^{729} forbids n^3 ≤ x (768 > 729). If n follows OOEOOEOOE, then T_OOEOOEOOE(n) < n^2 because y^{512} ≤ n^{729} forbids n^2 ≤ y (1024 > 729). A CE that follows OOEOOE follows OOEOOEOO. On MinimalNonTerm a completed third OOE cannot land even: an even landing below n^2 is descent. This is not a proof that the third residual is always OOE, not a PE theorem, and not a halt theorem.

If n ≥ 2 follows OOEOOEOOEOE, then T_OOEOOEOOEOE(n) < n^2 because w^{2048} ≤ n^{2187} forbids n^2 ≤ w (4096 > 2187). A CE that follows OOEOOEOOE follows OOEOOEOOEO. On MinimalNonTerm an even OE landing after a third OOE is descent. This is not a length-11 cycle census, not a proof that every escaped even drops, and not a halt theorem.

If n ≥ 2 follows OOEOOEOOEOEO, then T_OOEOOEOOEOEO(n) < n^2 because q^{4096} ≤ n^{6561} forbids n^2 ≤ q (8192 > 6561). A CE that follows OOEOOEOOEOE follows OOEOOEOOEOEO, and that image is odd. Another escaped even is impossible on this step. This is not a length-11 cycle census and not a halt theorem.

The itinerary OOEOOEOOEOEOO loses the square-cell gap (19683 > 16384). If n ≥ 2 follows that itinerary, then T(n) < n^3 because u^{8192} ≤ n^{19683} forbids n^3 ≤ u (24576 > 19683). A CE that follows OOEOOEOOEOE follows OOEOOEOOEOEOO. This is not a proof that the image stays below n^2, not a length-11 cycle census, and not a halt theorem.

If every CycleItinerary at m ≥ 2 is impossible, then any n ≥ 2 that does not reach 1 escapes to infinity. Bounded nontermination is eventual cycling, and a repeat of period at least 1 is a CycleItinerary at the repeated state. This does not prove that every cycle is impossible, does not prove that escape is impossible, and is not a halt theorem.

No n ≥ 2 realizes a Juggler cycle itinerary with at most three even letters (Paper A Theorem 3.22). Every CycleItinerary has a CycleMin rotation that starts OO, ends E, and is formally expanding; those itineraries are the odd-run family, the two-even leftovers (Theorem 3.12), the internal-E bootstrap, the seven bunched leftovers (Theorems 3.14–3.20), or the gapped leftovers (Theorems 3.13 and 3.21). The corollary is that a nontrivial cycle itinerary has length at least eleven (Paper A Corollary 3.23). Lean theorems no_cycle_itinerary_even_count_le_three and cycle_itinerary_length_ge_eleven in EvenCountThree.lean. This is an even-count assembler, not a length-9 or length-10 itinerary census, and not a halt theorem.

On a MinimalNonTerm or CycleMin start, the first even residual always overshoots: T(O^a E)(n) > n and the even residual sits at or above (n+1)^2. The return-to-n cell of the first-even dichotomy is an even-count-1 cycle itinerary, now excluded by no_cycle_itinerary_even_count_le_three. Lean theorems minimal_first_even_overshoots and cycleMin_first_even_overshoots in EvenCountThree.lean. This sharpens the leftover start. It is not a four-even exclusion, not a halt theorem, and not a ReturnBelow law.

On a CycleMin start n ≥ 2 the cycle maximum satisfies (n+1)^2 ≤ M. Equivalently, on a CycleMax the rotated minimum m satisfies (m+1)^2 ≤ M, so T(M) > m. The first-cell family m^2 < M < (m+1)^2 is impossible. cycle_distinguished_order_succ_sq is the distinguished-order package with that scale. Corollary of cycleMin_first_even_overshoots: the first even residual already sits at or above (n+1)^2 and is a cycle state. Lean: cycleMin_max_ge_succ_sq, cycleMax_min_succ_sq_le, cycleMax_landing_gt_min, cycleMax_exists_min_succ_sq, cycle_distinguished_order_succ_sq in EvenCountThree.lean. Not a first-cell census, not a leftover exclusion, and not a halt theorem. Not imported by JugglerPaper.

On a CycleMin word that ends O^a E with a ≥ 1 and the preceding letter not odd, the last odd-run has length exactly one. Equivalently, a CycleMin word cannot end O^a E for a ≥ 2. This is no_cycleMin_odd_run when the prefix is empty and no_cycleMin_bootstrap_last_gap after an internal even: oo_suffix_threshold at the last valley versus the last-even one-step preimage, the OOEOOE sandwich of Theorem 3.6. Every CycleMin word ends O^a E with a ≤ 1; a = 0 is a trailing even run of length at least two and is not excluded. Lean: exists_trailing_odds, cycleMin_not_last_odd_run_ge_two, cycleMin_last_odd_run_eq_one, exists_cycleMin_last_odd_run in EvenCountThree.lean. Not a forced-OE incoming side, not a leftover-killer, and not a halt theorem. Not imported by JugglerPaper.

A residual-shaped word O^a E^b is formally expanding iff 2^{a+b}<3^a. For a≥1 this is equivalent to a+b ≤ log₂(3^a), or b ≤ maxExpandingEvens(a). In particular a=2 or 3 forces b≤1, and a=4 forces b≤2. This is the syntactic expanding language, not a realized-orbit theorem.

For n≥2, PersistentOddResidual x y if and only if PersistentExpandingResidual x y. A contracting residual cannot overshoot, and 2^k=3^o is impossible for a nonempty residual. The expanding qualifier of a persistent residual is therefore redundant.

The expanding residual word grammar, or a finite residue-mod-8 successor automaton, is an independent obstruction to an infinite persistent expanding chain. Counterexamples: on n≥2 persistence already is expansion, so the attack reduces to T_w(n)>n; the OOE type self-loop 365→763→1749 exits odd-to-even at 4447; every odd class modulo 8 both continues and leaves the PE frontier. A finite run bound M is not proved and is not supplied by this grammar.

The integer exponent surplus of a finite Juggler word is E(w)=3^{#O(w)}-2^{|w|}, and E(w)>0 if and only if the itinerary is formally expanding. An expanding residual block O^a E^b with b≥1 has b<a. On an expanding itinerary, n^{3^{#O}}=n^{2^{|w|}+E(w)}. Relative slack multiplies under concatenation, and the slack numerator of a three-block word is n^{3^{o(v)+o(w)}}. The chain 365 --OOE--> 763 --OOE--> 1749 --OOE--> 4447 is a PersistentExpansionChain. This does not bound consecutive expanding persistent runs.

For a realized Juggler itinerary, the pair (A,B)=(3^{#O(w)}, 2^{|w|}) multiplies under concatenation, and n^A = T_w(n)^B + Δ_w(n). The 1+q concatenation law is the same identity in multiplier coordinates: 1+q_{uv} = (1+q_u)^{A_v} (1+q_v)^{B_u}. In logarithms this is log T = λ log n - c and the weighted cocycle y_m = Λ_m y_0 - C_m with B_m = C_m/Λ_m. The local comparison c < (λ-1) log n is T_w(n) > n on an expanding itinerary. These are the existing slack identities, not a new obstruction.

Four consecutive persistent expanding Juggler residual blocks exist: 1999 follows OOE to 5169, 5169 follows OOOOEE to 50093, 50093 follows OOE to 193753, and 193753 follows OOE to 887471. Each step is PersistentExpandingResidual.

Positive local slack, after the exact expansion weights, puts a nontrivial upper bound on the density or run length of expanding persistent residual blocks independently of T_w(n)≥n. In particular there is a uniform ε>0 with c/(λ-1)≥ε on every expanding persistent block, or the normalized budget B_m is bounded below independently of the endpoint tautology B_m≤y_0(1-1/Λ_m). Counterexamples: the OOE block at 180370579261640036336071806107777 has 0<q<10^{-30}; B_m/B_taut reaches 10^{-9} on the n≤4000 window; a length-5 all-expanding persistent run starts at 2183.

Fate classes of the Juggler map are backward-closed (J n ∈ A ⟹ n ∈ A): the starts that reach 1 (reachesOne_backwardClosed), the starts that do not (not_reachesOne_backwardClosed), the basin Ancestor · m of any state m (ancestor_backwardClosed), and the divergent starts (escapes_backwardClosed); R and the divergent set are also forward-closed (reachesOne_floorPower, escapes_floorPower). Every start n ≥ 1 reaches 1, or is an ancestor of a state m ≥ 2 on a cycle (Periodic m), or escapes (fate_trichotomy, from cycles_or_escapes), and the fates exclude one another: a start that reaches 1 or enters a cycle has a bounded orbit (reachesOne_bounded, cycle_basin_bounded, reachesOne_not_escapes, cycle_basin_not_escapes), and a start that reaches 1 is not an ancestor of a cycle state m ≥ 2 (reachesOne_not_cycle_basin). Lemma 1.1 of the fate-contagion note. Not a halt theorem.

The two exact productions of a backward-closed set A. Even block: if m ∈ A then every even n with m·m ≤ n < (m+1)(m+1) has J n = m (floorPower_even_block) and lies in A (even_block_mem); the block has at least m even elements (even_block_card). OE fiber: Nat.sqrt (Nat.sqrt N) = m ⟺ m^4 ≤ N < (m+1)^4 (sqrt_sqrt_eq_iff, the exact form of the transparent nesting ⌊√⌊n^{3/2}⌋⌋ = ⌊n^{3/4}⌋); hence an odd n with m^4 ≤ n^3 < (m+1)^4 and even ⌊n^{3/2}⌋ = Nat.sqrt (n^3) has J (J n) = m (floorPower_oe_fiber) and lies in A when m does (oe_fiber_mem); the fibers of distinct m are disjoint (oe_fiber_disjoint). Lemmas 2.1–2.2 of the fate-contagion note.

Odd generation of two-way closed fate classes (fate-contagion note, Theorem 6.1). Fate classes are forward-closed as well as backward-closed (ForwardClosed; reachesOne_forwardClosed, not_reachesOne_forwardClosed, escapes_forwardClosed; mem_iff_floorPower_mem). For a class A that is closed both ways with 1 ∉ A: every member n ≥ 1 descends by even steps only to an odd member of A (exists_odd_ancestor: ∃ k with floorPower^[k] n odd and in A, all earlier iterates even), that member is ≥ 3 (exists_odd_ancestor_ge_three), the odd members are exactly the odd preimages of A ∩ {⌊m^{3/2}⌋ : m odd} (odd_mem_iff: for odd n, A n ↔ A (Nat.sqrt (n^3))), and A is nonempty iff it contains ⌊m^{3/2}⌋ for some odd m ≥ 3 (nonempty_iff_odd_image_mem). Consequence: every positive integer reaches 1 iff no image ⌊m^{3/2}⌋ of an odd m fails to reach 1; the failure set is the E-forest over the odd preimages of F ∩ S. This is the exact skeleton of the S-fairness reformulation: the one free term of the first-letter decomposition (6.1) is the share of OO-type odd numbers whose image lies in F. Not a halt theorem.

Envelope descent into a certified floor. For a realized word w at n (follows n w), if n ^ 3^{#O(w)} ≤ N₀ ^ 2^{|w|} as integers then floorPower^[|w|] n ≤ N₀ (iterate_le_of_envelope, from power_bound_word and Nat.pow_le_pow_iff_left); if moreover every 1 ≤ m ≤ N₀ lies in a backward-closed class A, then n ∈ A (mem_of_envelope_floor); in particular, with A = ReachesOne and the realized itinerary of the first k steps, n ^ 3^{#O(itinerary n k)} ≤ N₀ ^ 2^k implies ReachesOne n (reachesOne_of_itinerary_envelope). This is the exact step of the Tao-type reduction: a start whose exponent walk reaches −L(y) = −log₂(log 2y / log N₀) within d steps enters [1, N₀]. Not a halt theorem.

Let x1 = T_{O^{a0} E}(n) and B = T_OE. If O^{a0} E follows at n, (OE)^r follows at x1, and B^r(x1) ≥ n, then 2^{2r+a0+1} ≤ 3^{a0+r}. Write R(a0) for the largest such r. Then R(2)=0, R(3)=1, R(4)=3. This is an AboveAnchor / isolated-prefix theorem, not a cycle-return theorem. On a CycleMin-shaped prefix this bounds isolated-OE transport before the first internal OO: r ≤ R(a0). In particular an a0=2 CycleMin cannot complete one OE after the first even while staying ≥ n, so its first internal OO, if it exists, is immediate (r=0). The same r=0 bound holds for a MinimalNonTerm realization of O^{2}E(OE)^r. Lean: isolatedOddSurvival_bound, isolated_oe_ge_implies_exponent, isolated_oe_lt_of_scale_gap, isolated_oe_r_max_two in FirstInternalOO.lean; aboveAnchor_isolated_two in MinimumRelative.lean; no_cycleMin_prefix_ooe_oe, cycleMin_isolated_two in CycleObstructions.lean; minimal_isolated_two in Minimal.lean. The suffix after that OO is not classified. This is not a Z5 family, not a length-11 census, and not a halt theorem.

Each of the four joint parity classes of (floor(n^{3/2}), floor(floor(n^{3/2})^{3/2})) over odd n ≤ N has cardinality N/8 + O(N^{23/24+eps}); in particular #{odd n ≤ N : J(n) odd, J^2(n) even} = N/8 + O(N^{23/24+eps}), one itinerary letter beyond the ambient odd-input bound. Proof: Vaaler wave expansion, the exact linearization row J-nested-parity-linearization, one van der Corput A-process at H = N^{1/12}, constant-gap cells with an exactly split moving-endpoint expansion, and the second-derivative test per cell; exponent deliberately unoptimized. Ambient counting over all odd starts; not an orbit transfer theorem, not a frequency theorem along trajectories, and not a termination claim. Imported into the parity-discrepancy paper as Theorem 4.4. Lean covers only the exact floor reductions (floor_gap_eq_carry gap cells, floor_odd_iff_half_le_fract_half parity bridge); the analytic estimate is a human proof.

Tier-2 bricks. Lemma M: for odd n ≥ 5, X = n^{3/2}, m = floor(X), integer G ≥ 0, Z = X + G: m^{3/2} = -(1/8)X^{3/2} + (3/4) m X^{1/2} + (3/8) m^2 X^{-1/2} + R5 and (m+G)^{3/2} = Z^{3/2} - (3/2)X Z^{1/2} + (3/8)X^2 Z^{-1/2} + m((3/2)Z^{1/2} - (3/4)X Z^{-1/2}) + (3/8) m^2 Z^{-1/2} + R6, with 0 ≤ R5, R6 ≤ (1/16)(base-1)^{-3/2} (positive third-order Taylor remainders). Lemma N: the level-2 gap satisfies g2 = v(n+2h) - v(n) = floor(DY) + [theta2 ≥ 1 - {DY}] with DY = Y(n+2h) - Y(n), Y = m^{3/2} — Lemma B one level up; on constant-g1 cells DY is a quadratic in m with smooth coefficients by Lemma M. Validated exactly to n = 10^{12} (Lemma M, gaps h in {1,2,5}) and on 3800 orbit samples (Lemma N). Bricks for the kernel bound, subsequently proved as Theorem R (row J-kernel-cancellation). Lean covers only the Lemma N floor identity (seq_floor_gap); Lemma M and all analytic content remain human proofs.

Theorem R (formerly Conjecture O; Theorem 5.3 of the parity-discrepancy paper): K_c(P) = sum over odd n ~ P of e(c(n) {floor(n^{3/2})^{3/2}}) with c(n) = (3k/4) n^{9/8} satisfies K_c(P) << P^{1-1/96+eps}, uniformly for 1 <= k <= P^{1/24}, deliberately unoptimized. The statement is the monomial; a two-sided scale c^{(r)} ~ k P^{9/8-r} does not determine the Step 5a cancellation. Proof (Phase 25 expansion, Phase 26 repair; Paper B Section 4): double Weyl differencing at H1 = P^{1/48}, H2 = P^{1/24}; the exact master identity DD(c theta_2) = (DD c) theta_2 + (D2 c)({W}-kappa_2) + (D1 c)({W'}-kappa_2') + c_11({DDY}-kappa''-D2 kappa_2), proved algebraically in the text by the product rule on the carry-branch decomposition; level-2 waves handled by Lemma 5.2's exact e(qY) model with third differencing (bottleneck P^{23/24}); offset branches by shifted-window expansion (Lemma 3.7) with the printed anchor composite 945/512 - 27/64; zero-offset middle band repaired in Phase 26 by global sublevel splitting (Lemma 3.9): a smooth three-term monomial model for f'' with a trivial bound on the transition set Omega_V and the second-derivative test on the good pieces, total << P^{15/16+eps} — the earlier per-cell summation of inverse-power van der Corput terms was incorrectly assembled and is withdrawn. All derivative tests on odd n are read through the parity-reindexing lemma (Lemma 3.10). Writeup repair (4 September 2026): Lemma 5.2b isolates the frozen-shape interpolant: local (cG) = -135/1024 k beta1 beta2 n^{-13/8} with beta frozen, global Lambda substitutes Delta_i X as values only; rho_0 ratios are O(P^{-1/4}) and sit under 1/2304. Zero-offset B = (9/32) k beta1 beta2 n^{-9/8} has constant size |B| <= 6 (the printed |B|<1 dropped h1 h2 from (C1)); Lemma 3.7 at T = P^{1/2} still applies. Theorem 5.3 exponent unchanged. Earlier writeup repair (2 September 2026): Lemma 5.2 coefficient budget enlarged to |q_d| <= 4 P^{1/24} with at most nine decorations (the printed |q_d| <= P^{1/16} overflowed at every census P with ratio 3 P^{-1/48} -> 0); Step 5b interpolant keeps the two-term majorant 219 P^{-25/24} + 0.11 P^{-5/6} and does not collapse to 0.1 P^{-5/6}; c7 = 1/288 is displayed for the printed triple; P0 is named and ineffective (windows ~ 3e5; V <= c7 S/2 of size 10^{24}). Numerical validators (master_identity_check, kernel_margin_scan) remain in the repository as checks, not proof steps.

Gap transfer (Paper A Theorem 4.10). On a Juggler CycleMin start n ≥ 2 with word w of length L and oddCount o, n · log n · min(o log 3 − L log 2, 1) ≤ 2 L (cycleMin_gap_transfer). Proof: Theorem 4.4 reads P(A − B) ≤ L A with A = 3^o, B = 2^L, P = n log n; if A ≤ B the left side is nonpositive, if A ≥ 2B then P ≤ 2L, and if B < A < 2B then Λ = log(A/B) ≤ (A − B)/B and P(A − B)/B ≤ LA/B ≤ 2L. Abstract form cycleMin_length_of_gap: any ε ≤ min(Λ, 1) gives n log n · ε ≤ 2L. Floor-free; the classical transcendence input is a hypothesis, not a Lean theorem. Not a halt theorem and not a period bound at any floor.

For every realized finite Juggler word w, n^{3^{#O(w)}} = T_w(n)^{2^{|w|}} + Δ_w(n), where Δ is the recursively lifted accumulation of local floor remainders. Δ ≥ 0, so the power envelope is a corollary; Δ = 0 iff every local remainder vanishes; concatenation is the two-term power-gap lift, not an additive sum.

For every natural n and finite parity itinerary w, follows n w if and only if the actual length-|w| Juggler itinerary of n equals w. The itinerary image equals the |w|-fold iterate, and images and realization compose under word concatenation.
If n and m realize the same finite Juggler word w and n ≤ m, then the image of n after w is at most the image of m after w.

If u and v are expanding itineraries (2^{|u|} < 3^{#O(u)} and 2^{|v|} < 3^{#O(v)}), then u ++ v is expanding: 2^{|u|+|v|} = 2^{|u|} 2^{|v|} < 3^{#O(u)} 3^{#O(v)}. A concatenation of expanding residual blocks is never an exponent-gap certificate. This is not a finite PE-run bound and not a halt theorem.

T(x)=m if and only if m²≤F(x)<(m+1)², with F(x)=x on the even branch and F(x)=x³ on the odd branch. The landing gap ρ=F(x)-m² satisfies 0≤ρ<2T(x)+1. Odd landing is membership of F(x) in a union of odd-m one-step preimages. These are the existing inverse-floor and remainder-window lemmas under landing names.

The normalized landing position θ=ρ/(2T+1) is a compact state for persistent odd-to-odd continuation: it occupies a proper subinterval of [0,1], or a coarse θ-bin predicts the next landing parity better than a residue class, or θ(T(x)) is a function of θ(x) and the branch. Counterexamples: on odd n≤2000, odd-odd θ occupies [0,0.997] and every tenth of [0,1]; PE-continuation landings span [0,0.995]; next-parity entropy given a θ-bin is ≈0.99, matching x mod 8; θ→θ transitions fill essentially all bins.

If y is odd and T(y) is odd, then the local remainder ρ=y³-T(y)² satisfies ρ≡y-1 (mod 8). Consequently v₂(ρ)=1 when y≡3 or 7 (mod 8), v₂(ρ)=2 when y≡5 (mod 8), and v₂(ρ)≥3 when y≡1 (mod 8) and ρ≠0. The same congruences hold for any odd square below y³; the floor T(y)=⌊y^{3/2}⌋ is not used beyond selecting an odd landing.

Persistent-expanding residual history forces a 2-adic landing restriction stronger than y mod 8: either v₂(y³-T(y)²)≥r>1 at a PE endpoint, or y≡1 (mod 16) forces v₂≥4, or the valuation locks the next residual word. Counterexamples: 365 maps to the PE endpoint 763 with v₂=1; 33≡1 (mod 16) has v₂=3; on odd n≤4000 the PE valuation table is the residue law, and v₂=1 continues as both persistent OOE and non-persistent OOEE.

OOOOOOEEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary at any n ≥ 2. The argument is an exhaustive evaluation for n < 128 together with the three-even cell z < (n+1)^8 against the coarse lower envelope n^{729} > 2^{1330}(n+1)^{512} for n ≥ 128. The computational prefix-cell first fires at N0 = 73; 128 is the algebraic cutoff. This excludes that one three-even leftover only; it is not a length-9 census, not an exclusion of the remaining eight leftovers, and not a halt theorem. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_ooooooeee.

For every k ≥ 6 and every n ≥ 2, the even-terminating two-even leftover O^{k-2}EE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. Large n uses the shared tail n^{3^{k-2}} > 2^{e_{k-2}}(n+1)^{2^k} at the uniform algebraic cutoff n ≥ 256, obtained by cubing the length-6 comparison; e_a = 2(3^a-2^a) = log2(lowerDenom(O^a)). Below 256 the argument is the existing k=6,7 leftovers, a Fin 256 table at k=8, and the fact that n ≥ 2 does not follow seven consecutive odds. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_two_even_ee. This excludes that one family only; it is not a length-8 census and not a halt theorem.

For every k ≥ 6 and every n ≥ 2, the leftover O^{k-3}EOE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. The last-odd cube trick plus (y+1)^3 < 2(n+1)^4 reduces to the same shared tail as O^{k-2}EE. Large n is n ≥ 256; below 256 the argument is the existing k=6,7 leftovers, Fin 256 tables at k=8,9, and the seven-odd obstruction for k ≥ 10. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_two_even_eoe. This excludes that one family only; it is not a length-8 census and not a halt theorem.

For every n ≥ 2, a ≥ 2, and b ≥ 4, the gapped three-even leftover O^a E O^b EE is not a Juggler CycleMin at n. CycleMin puts the remainder O^b EE at y = T_{O^a E}(n) ≥ n. The leftover cell is measured against n, so y ≥ n tightens it against the shared two-even tail at y. Large y is the uniform cutoff y ≥ 256; below 256 the argument is seven consecutive odds on the prefix or the remainder, or a Fin 256 table on the short-gap window 2 ≤ a ≤ 6, 4 ≤ b ≤ 6. Lean theorem no_cycleMin_gapped_three_even_ee. This excludes gapped CycleMins only; it is not a CycleItinerary theorem at a non-minimum start, not a bunched-tail attack, not a length-8 or length-9 census, and not a halt theorem.

For every n ≥ 2, a ≥ 2, and b ≥ 3, the gapped three-even leftover O^a E O^b EOE is not a Juggler CycleMin at n. The same first-E transport applies: y ≥ n tightens the leftover cell against the shared two-even tail at y, using the last-odd cube reduction already used for O^{k-3}EOE. Large y is y ≥ 256; below 256 the argument is seven-odd or a Fin 256 table on 2 ≤ a ≤ 6, 3 ≤ b ≤ 6. Lean theorem no_cycleMin_gapped_three_even_eoe. This excludes gapped CycleMins only; it is not a CycleItinerary theorem at a non-minimum start, not a bunched-tail attack, not a length-8 or length-9 census, and not a halt theorem.

For every a ≥ 6 and every n ≥ 2, the bunched leftover O^a EEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. Large n uses the three-even cell z < (n+1)^8 against C_{O^a}, which is the tail n^{3^a} > 2^{e_a}(n+1)^{2^{a+3}} at the algebraic cutoff n ≥ 128, obtained by cubing the OOOOOOEEE comparison; e_a = 2(3^a-2^a) = log2(lowerDenom(O^a)). Below 128 the argument is the existing a=6 table and the fact that n ≥ 2 does not follow seven consecutive odds. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_three_even_eee. This excludes that one bunched family only; it is not the other six bunched tails, not a length-8 or length-9 census, and not a halt theorem.

For every a ≥ 5 and every n ≥ 2, the bunched leftover O^a EOEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. For n ≥ 4 the mixed cell is z < (n+1)^6: two trailing evens give p < (n+1)^4, the one-odd envelope gives y^3 ≤ 4p^2, and n ≥ 4 upgrades that to y < (n+1)^3. Large n at a = 5 uses the tail n^{3^a} > 2^{e_a}(n+1)^{6·2^a} at the algebraic cutoff n ≥ 314, obtained by persisting the comparison at 314 and cubing in a; e_a = 2(3^a-2^a). At a = 6 the same cell already fires at n ≥ 16. Below those cutoffs the argument is the a = 5 table, the a = 6 table, and seven consecutive odds. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_three_even_eoee. This excludes that one bunched family only; a uniform coarse (n+1)^K cell for all six remaining bunched families is false; it is not a length-8 or length-9 census and not a halt theorem.

For every a ≥ 4 and every n ≥ 2, the bunched leftover O^a EOOEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. For n ≥ 32 the mixed cell is z < (n+1)^4: two trailing evens give p < (n+1)^4, the two-odd envelope gives y^9 ≤ 1024 p^4, and n ≥ 32 upgrades that to y < (n+1)^2. The resulting comparison is the shared two-even tail at length a+2, which holds for n ≥ 256. Below 256 the argument is Fin 256 tables at a = 4,5,6 and seven consecutive odds thereafter. Lean theorem no_cycle_itinerary_three_even_eooee. This excludes that one bunched family only; it is not a length-8 or length-9 census and not a halt theorem.

For every a ≥ 3 and every n ≥ 2, the bunched leftover O^a EOOOEE is not a Juggler cycle itinerary. For a ≥ 4 and n ≥ 3 the mixed cell is z < (n+1)^4: two trailing evens give p < (n+1)^4, the three-odd envelope gives y^{27} ≤ 2^{38} p^8, and n ≥ 3 upgrades that to y < (n+1)^2. The exponent walk of any Juggler orbit satisfies u_t = o_t log2(3) - t ≡ o_t · alpha (mod 1), alpha = log2(3) - 1 = log2(3/2), because t and o_t are integers and log2(3) = 1 + alpha. Along a cycle of period L the odd count o_t takes every value 0..o, so the walk values mod 1 are exactly the rotation orbit {j·alpha}, j < o. Largest gap mod 1: 5.194e-6 at L = 478245 (o = 301739), 5.101e-6 at L = 780239 (o = 492276), 5.008e-6 at L = 1082233 (o = 682813). This is Paper A's Ostrowski layer read mod 1; it is not a period bound and not a halt theorem.

The E-tree of a seed m occupies, at generation k, the integers from m^(2^k) to (m+1)^(2^k) with internal density 2^(-k), hence natural density about 1/m at that scale, for every k. Verified exactly: m = 101, k = 1 gives 101 members at scale 1.0404e4 (density 0.009708); k = 2 gives 1040603 members at scale 1.0824e8 (density 0.009614), against 1/m = 0.009901. The burst scales of a seed are m^(2^k), one per generation.

Write c(x) = log2 log x. The scales carrying E-tree bursts of a backward-closed class are c(m) + k over its seeds m and k >= 0, so the covered scales mod 1 are {c(m) mod 1}. By J-lachesis-walk-rotation and J-lachesis-loglog-clock the cycle states of a Lachesis basin sit at c(n) + u_t, an equidistributed rotation orbit with largest gap 5.101e-6 at L = 780239, far finer than the 1.7e-4 clock defect and both far below 1. A dyadic block is a c-window of width about 1 / log y (1.46e-2 at y = 1e30, 4.34e-4 at y = 1e1000), so some cycle state's pure-E burst lands in every block out to log y = 1/5.101e-6, that is y < 1e85142; beyond that the alpha-gaps reopen. Bursts begin at n^2 (generation 1 of the minimum) and none exist below it; the full rotation is available only once c(y) - c(n) >= 1 + u_max, u_max = log2(ln M / ln n) >= 1 the cycle's walk height (Paper A: M >= (n+1)^2). Hence a Lachesis basin is not lacunary on the range n^(2^(1 + u_max)) <= y < 1e85142: it carries natural density at least about 1/n on every dyadic block there, n the cycle minimum; at n = 3.5e8 the threshold is 1e34 for u_max = 1, 1e69 for u_max = 2, 1e137 for 3. The first draft omitted the threshold. This is the third case, missing from contagion note Sec.5.3, which treats only the single seed (lacunary) and the interval [1, N0] (uniform); for the Lachesis class it upgrades Corollary 4.3 from some y in a range to every dyadic block. No fate is excluded and no period bound moves; not a halt theorem. Consolidated into the contagion note Sec. 5.3 (5 Sep 2026) as the third seed-set case, between the single point (lacunary) and the interval [1, N0] (uniform), with the exact half Lean and the every-block half labelled CONJECTURE there. Paper C is untouched; Paper A is untouched (AGENTS.md forbids editing it from a Phase-0 branch).

J-lachesis-walk-rotation does not know whether the orbit closes: the clock positions of a divergent orbit's states below y are the rotation orbit {c(n) + j alpha : j <= O(y)}, O(y) the odd count before the walk first exceeds u(y) = log2(ln y / ln n). Its basin has an E-burst in the block at y iff a point of that orbit lies within 1/ln y of c(y) mod 1; sufficient is gap(O(y)) <= 1/ln y, gap(O) the largest gap of {j alpha mod 1 : j <= O}, non-increasing in O. Thresholds O*(y) = min{O : gap(O) <= 1/ln y}: 40 at 1e12, 146 at 1e30, 252 at 1e50, 305 at 1e68, 358 at 1e100, 1635 at 1e300, 12275 at 1e1000 (O gap(O) swings between 1.26 and 6.56 with the continued fraction of alpha, three-distance). The gate is meaningful only for u(y) >= log2 3, i.e. y >= n^3: the hug band [0, log2 3) is the minimal invariant band of the walk (Lean hug_band_step_exists, narrow_band_dead, dead_zone_nonempty), and below 1 no even step is possible and at most one odd step fits (no_even_step_below_one, odd_steps_below_one_le_one), so for y < n^3 every orbit has O(y) <= 2 < O*(y) and no basin is every-block there; at n = 3.5e8 the 1e12 row (u = 0.49) is vacuous. Translated to the orbit: it must reach u(y) in at least O*(y) odd steps, so its odd share up to scale y must lie in the window (q*, s*(y)) with s* - q* = 0.0049 at 1e12, 0.0039 at 1e68, 0.0040 at 1e100, 0.0002 at 1e1000. The all-odd rate 0.585 is far outside the window at every scale. The p = 19 hug near-return rate, theta_19 / 12 = 0.00163 walk per odd step, is inside up to 1e300 but outside at 1e1000, where the gate is 0.00056; the p = 84 rate theta_84 / 53 = 5.7e-5 is inside everywhere tested (p = 1054 gives 9.5e-8). So the gate tightens with y and pushes a persistent escaper down the near-return spectrum 19, 84, 1054, ... - the cycle-period ladder of flight note Sec. 6. A Clotho basin is every-block at scale y exactly when the divergent orbit is a critical-share escaper up to that scale hugging a deep enough near-return - the kind the flight extract lets persist; a fast escaper has a lacunary basin, like a single seed. The density is then about (K / ln y) times the partial inverse sum over the states below y, K in [1, 3]; that partial sum is at least 1/n and, unlike the cycle's, is not pinned by finance. Excludes no fate; not a halt theorem.

fract_mul_sub_nat_eq_fract_mul_sub_one: for every real x and naturals o, t, Int.fract (o x - t) = Int.fract (o (x - 1)). Instance fract_walk_eq_fract_rotation: the exponent walk walk o t = o log2 3 - t satisfies Int.fract (walk o t) = Int.fract (o alphaClock) with alphaClock = log2 3 - 1 = log2 (3/2); corollary fract_walk_depends_only_on_odd_count: two prefixes with the same odd count have the same walk mod 1 whatever their lengths. So along any orbit - cycle, divergent, or terminating - the walk values mod 1 are the rotation orbit {j alphaClock} indexed by the odd count. The exact half of J-lachesis-walk-rotation; the gap sizes of the rotation orbit remain a computation. No sorry.

even_chain_mem_burst: if the first k states of the orbit of n are even and floorPower^[k] n = m, then m^(2^k) <= n < (m + 1)^(2^k); proved by induction from the one-step cell Nat.sqrt n ^ 2 <= n < (Nat.sqrt n + 1) ^ 2 (sqrt_cell) and floorPower_even_eq. Corollary even_chain_log_offset (1 <= m): 2^k log m <= log n < 2^k log (m + 1), i.e. in the clock c = log2 log the chain sits at offset exactly k above [c(m), c(m+1)). This is the interval half of J-lachesis-etree-density; the count of the chain (about m^(2^k - 1) even integers) is not formalized. No sorry.

WalkStep u v := v = u + alphaClock or v = u - 1. hug_band_step_exists: from any u in [0, 1 + alphaClock) some step stays in the band. narrow_band_dead: if w - alphaClock <= u < 1 then no step from u stays in [0, w); dead_zone_nonempty: for 0 < w < 1 + alphaClock such a u exists in [0, w) - so the hug band [0, log2 3) is the minimal invariant band of the exponent walk. no_even_step_below_one and odd_steps_below_one_le_one (from half_lt_alphaClock, i.e. 9 > 8): below 1 no even step is possible and at most one odd step fits. Supporting bounds one_lt_logb_two_three, logb_two_three_lt_two. These are the exact reasons the Clotho every-block gate is vacuous for y < n^3 and the Lachesis bursts begin at n^2. No sorry.

Inside the hug band the parity letter is forced. band_step_forced_odd: from u < 1 a step staying in [0, 1 + alphaClock) must be the odd one, v = u + alphaClock (the even step goes negative). band_step_forced_even: from 1 <= u it must be the even one, v = u - 1 (the odd step exceeds the band). band_successor_unique: a band-confined walk has exactly one admissible successor at every point. So the walk of a band-confined orbit is the lift of the rotation by alphaClock and its parity word is the mechanical (Sturmian) word of that rotation - the hug itinerary - determined by the starting walk alone, with no freedom. No sorry.

How long a descent-free flight can stay in the hug band [0, log2 3) is the hug-prefix-realization question, already CLOSE (juggler_hug_prefix_realization). By J-loglog-clock-band-word-forced-lean the band word is forced, so staying in the band for L steps means realizing one specific prefix of length L - the mechanical word of the rotation by log2(3/2). The recorded census says the extremal hug cylinder tracks 2^(-L) on [3, 2e8] with fill to depth 28, and log2(2e8) = 27.6: band residence is exactly the fair-coin maximum log2 N over N starts, with no anomaly. The pigeonhole bound of J-clotho-hug-excess-rate (a flight with walk in [0, B) has distinct states in [n, n^(2^B)), hence leaves or cycles within n^(2^B) = n^3 steps at the hug band, about 4e25 at the floor) is therefore off by the whole scale: reality is log2 n, roughly 28. The residence question is not a new branch and must not be reopened as one; the missing object remains a rate, not a bound.

not_reachesOne_even_chain_ge: if n >= 1 does not reach 1 and its first k states are even, then 261^(2^k) <= n. Proof: the k-th iterate is again a failure (backwardClosed_iterate with reachesOne_backwardClosed), hence >= 261 by the Lean floor (reachesOne_of_lt_two_hundred_sixty_one via not_reachesOne_ge; positivity by floorPower_iterate_pos), and the even chain multiplies exponents (even_chain_mem_burst). At the certified floor N0 = 3.5e8 the same argument gives (N0 + 1)^(2^k) (verified computation, not Lean): the failure set is purely odd on (N0, (N0+1)^2), and its E^k-cylinder is empty below (N0+1)^(2^k). The depth-k form of the fate note's 'min F is an OO-start'. Not a halt theorem; F is not shown empty.

One visibility law for the three fates: for a backward-closed class with seed set S0 (its minimal elements), the E-visible natural density on the block at scale y is about (K / ln y) times the sum of 1/x over the seeds whose bursts land there, K in [1, 2]. Atropos: S0 = [1, N0], bursts tile, sum about ln N0 = 19.7, density about 0.06 at 1e68 - contagion note Sec. 5.3's log N0 / (2 log y) recovered. Lachesis: S0 = the cycle, a rotation orbit with gaps 5e-6, sum in [theta(L) ln n, L/n] by Lean finance, density [4e-7, 4e-5] at 1e68 for y >= n^(2^(1 + u_max)). Clotho: S0 = the orbit's states below y, a rotation orbit of length O(y), every-block only under slow escape. The certified floor's own E-forest is therefore 1e4..1e5 times more visible than any finance-surviving cycle at every block: the quantitative reason the census sees R and nothing else. Everything here bounds fate classes from below; the upper bound is the free term (J-lachesis-upper-bound-free-term), and nothing moves the pressure form. A persistent slow escaper sits at odd share in (q*, q* + 0.004), on the pressure threshold from above, measure zero as a single thread.

AboveAnchor(n,w) means n follows w and every T^i(n) for i ≤ |w| is at least n. CycleMin(n,w) implies AboveAnchor(n,w). MinimalNonTerm(n) implies AboveAnchor(n,w) for every realized finite prefix w. A realized image T_w(n) < n is FiniteProgress. If the image is even and below n^2, one more even letter is FiniteProgress (the k=1 case of T(x) < n^k when x is even and x < n^{2k}). An AboveAnchor prefix plus ReturnBelow at the image is FiniteProgress. This is not cycle closure, not a no-cycle theorem, and not a halt theorem.

If n ≥ 2 and n^2 ≤ x < n^3, then an even x resets to n ≤ T(x) < n^2, and an odd x lifts to T(x) ≥ n^3. Even x < n^3 already gives T(x) < n^2 because n^3 < n^4. If that next image is also even, two even letters are FiniteProgress. On MinimalNonTerm a cube-cell even landing has odd next image. This is not a claim that a cube-cell even landing drops, not a next-letter envelope, and not a halt theorem.

If n ≥ 2 and n^2 ≤ x < n^3 with x odd, then n^3 ≤ T(x) < n^5 and T(x)^2 < n^9. If T(x) is even, the first return satisfies n ≤ T^2(x) < x < n^3 and T^2(x)^4 < n^9. If T(x) is odd, then x < T^2(x) and n^4 ≤ T^2(x). An even reset that is itself even and already below n^2 is FiniteProgress; on MinimalNonTerm that case is impossible. This is not a claim that every even reset lands below n^2, not a new integer-power census, and not a halt theorem.

If x is odd and T(x) is even, then T^2(x) < n^2 if and only if x^3 < n^8. This is the mixed odd-cube / even-square cell. It is strictly sharper than composing a cube-band bound x < n^3 into T^2(x)^4 < n^9. An eighth-cell even lift that returns even is FiniteProgress; on MinimalNonTerm that return is odd. This is not a claim that every leftover landing stays below n^8, not a defect restriction, and not a halt theorem.

The local Juggler remainder satisfies 0≤ρ<2T+1, hence η=ρ/T^2 < 2/T + 1/T^2 and 1+η < ((T+1)/T)^2. For the mixed itinerary OOE, 1+q = (1+η0)^3 (1+η1)^2 (1+η2)^4, and 1+q is strictly below the successor-ratio product ((T0+1)/T0)^6 ((T1+1)/T1)^4 ((T2+1)/T2)^8. The same bound at a successor start y depends only on the itinerary of y.

On realized odd-odd OOE starts, the last even remainder dominates the relative slack, and q_OOE(n) has order n^{-9/8}. After 329 follows OOOOOOOOE to y≈1.80·10^{32}, the next OOE block has 0<q<10^{-30} with q/y^{-9/8}≈2.64. Persistent expanding pairs have OOE-sequel q2 tracking y^{-9/8}. Large λ reduces successor q only by inflating y.

If a realized mixed itinerary has q_w(n)→0 then the itinerary converges to an exact rigid monochrome tower. Counterexample: the mixed itinerary OOE at 180370579261640036336071806107777 has 0<q<10^{-30}. Exact equality rigidity has no naive quantitative stability theorem.

For a realized Juggler itinerary, the relative slack 1+q = n^{3^{#O(w)}} / T_w(n)^{2^{|w|}} multiplies under concatenation: 1+q_{uv} = (1+q_u)^{3^{#O(v)}} (1+q_v)^{2^{|u|}}. An even letter multiplies by (1+η)^{2^k}; an odd letter multiplies by (1+q)^3 (1+η)^{2^k}. Running 1+q does not decrease under a realized extension. The surplus ratio R=Δ/S satisfies R≤1 iff T_w(n)≥n whenever S>0, so R is the endpoint comparison in other coordinates. A realized return T_w(n)=n uses the whole formal surplus.

If n ≥ 2 follows the Juggler word O^7, then T^7(n) ≥ (n+1)^16. In particular the EEEE inverse cell [n^16, (n+1)^16) is empty of seven-odd images, so O^7 EEEE is not a cycle itinerary. Lean theorems o7_image_ge_succ_pow16 and no_cycle_itinerary_oooooooeeee in O7EEEEGap.lean. Proof: no_follows_seven_odds_of_lt256 excludes n < 256; on an O^7 run the exact cells x_k^3 < (x_{k+1}+1)^2 and x_k ≥ n compose to n^{6177} < (n+1)^{3990} (T^7(n)+1)^{128}; for n ≥ 256 one has n^{6177} > (n+1)^{6038} because 257^{256} < 3·256^{256} and 256^{139} > 2^{40} > 3^{24} > (257/256)^{6038}. This replaces the leftover 4-fudge (first fire at 828484409) by the exact successor cell. Not a length-11 census and not a halt theorem. Not imported by JugglerPaper.

Write oddLanding y for y odd and T(y) odd, and oddRun 0 y = oddLanding y, oddRun (r+1) y = oddLanding y and oddRun r (T(y)). Then oddRun (r+1) y if and only if y is odd and oddRun r (T(y)). The odd-landing cylinder of a fixed m contains at most one integer.

The iterated odd-landing sets P_r occupy shrinking arithmetic cylinders, or iteration is recognized modulo 2^m, or successive square-gap coordinates on long odd runs are constrained. Counterexamples: on odd n≤8000 the stay fraction |P_{r+1}|/|P_r| is 0.49–0.53 through r=7; P_r is mostly isolated odds; every residue modulo 64 both continues and exits; θ on P_r and on the exit from P_{r-1} both occupy [0,1].

Not a cycle obstruction and not a halt theorem.

For every n ≥ 2, every a ≥ 6, and every prefix u, the itinerary u ++ O^a EEE is not a Juggler CycleMin at n. CycleMin puts the leftover at y = T_u(n) ≥ n. The leftover cell is measured against n, so y ≥ n tightens it against the EEE tail at y. Large y is y ≥ 256. Below 256, no start follows the leftover and lands in [2, y] (Fin 256 returnsIntoB table at a = 6; seven consecutive odds on the remainder for a ≥ 7). The case y = n reduces to no_cycle_itinerary_three_even_eee. Lean theorem no_cycleMin_prefix_eee. This excludes that one last-cluster class only; it is not a CycleItinerary theorem at a non-minimum start, not a bunched-short attack, not a length-11 census, and not a halt theorem.

Flight envelope on open descent-free prefixes: the Paper A Theorem 5.3 transport ported from minimum-based cycles to AboveAnchor, plus the anchor-free upper side. If AboveAnchor(n,w) with n >= 400 then for every k <= |w|, in log form, w_k (log n − Δ) <= log x_k <= w_k log n, where w_k = 3^{a_k}/2^k is the walk weight and Δ = 1.05 e/n + 0.7 o/(n√n) is the transport deficit over the full itinerary (aboveAnchor_transport, aboveAnchor_flight_envelope, WalkTransport.lean). The upper side is the log form of power_bound_word and needs only follows(n,w) with n >= 1 (follows_log_le_walkWeight): floors only lose, so every realized peak satisfies log H <= w_P log n with no anchor. The lower side is the cycleMin_transport induction verbatim with the cycle hypothesis replaced by the anchor hypothesis: odd injections priced at x_j >= n (aboveAnchor_iterate_ge), even injections at x_j >= n² (even_ge_sq_of_aboveAnchor), walk nonnegativity from aboveAnchor_prefix_pow_le (one_le_walkWeight_aboveAnchor). Consequence: the fly exponent Φ = log H / log n of an ascent prefix equals its peak walk weight w_P up to O(w_P Δ / log n). Sharpness audit (COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED, float diagnostics): through 2·10^4 zero violations of either side and worst transport-applicable relative fly excess 1.61·10^{-4}; on the seven high-flyers (peaks to 6.49·10^6 bits) the floors shave at most 0.014 bits off the ideal peak, Φ = w_P to relative 10^{-9}; 19.6% of odd starts peak after first descent and are priced only by the anchor-free upper side. Constrains realized ascent prefixes and hypothetical descent-free flights only: not a halt theorem, not a divergence theorem, and not a cycle obstruction.

Walk-height law (divergence rate) on descent-free prefixes: if AboveAnchor(n,w) with n >= 400 and the exponent walk is at height >= B doublings at step k (2^(k+B) <= 3^{a_k} with a_k the odd count of the k-prefix), then 2^B (log n − D) <= log x_k with the transport deficit D = 1.05 e/n + 0.7 o/(n√n); exponentiating, x_k >= (n e^{−D})^{2^B} — heights along a descent-free prefix are doubly exponential in the walk height (aboveAnchor_height_of_walk, weight form two_pow_le_walkWeight, WalkTransport.lean). One-case composition of aboveAnchor_transport with 2^B <= w_k = 3^{a_k}/2^k; when log n < D the bound is vacuously true since x_k >= 1. Appearing corollary of the September 2026 re-rooting of transport on AboveAnchor: composed with the flight walk-divergence theorem (J-flight-walk-divergence, human pigeonhole glue), every descent-free flight realizes this rate along an unbounded walk, so a divergent orbit escapes doubly exponentially in its walk height. Nonvacuous while D < log n (prefix lengths up to order n log n / 1.05); constrains descent-free prefixes only — not a halt theorem, not a divergence theorem, not a cycle obstruction.
